#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Upgrade OS only: host -> instance; never replicate user/agent subvolumes.
set -euo pipefail
fail() { printf 'sync-instance-upgrade: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ $# == 2 && $1 =~ ^(pair|sync|boot)$ && $2 =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,62}$ ]] || fail 'usage: sync-instance-upgrade pair|sync|boot NAME'
action=$1 name=$2
[[ $(id -u) == 0 ]] || fail 'host root required'
incus() { command incus --force-local "$@"; }
for tool in jq btrfs blkid findmnt losetup mount umount flock incus stat realpath blockdev lsblk awk find head; do
    command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || fail "missing $tool"
done
umask 077
pool=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool
[[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSROOT) == /@3tched-leaf-pool ]] || fail 'leaf pool not mounted'
receipt=$pool/.provisioning/$name.json
[[ -f $receipt && ! -L $receipt ]] || fail 'preparation receipt required'
jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg image "$pool/$name.img" \
    '.phase=="filesystems-prepared" and .name==$name and .image==$image and .filesystem_prepared==true' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail 'disk not prepared'
image=$pool/$name.img
[[ -f $image && ! -L $image && $(stat -c %i "$image") == "$(jq -r .image_inode "$receipt")" && $(stat -c %s "$image") == "$(jq -r .image_bytes "$receipt")" ]] || fail 'image pins differ'
exec 8>"$pool/.provisioning/host-upgrade.lock"
flock -n 8 || fail 'host upgrade transfer active'
exec 9>"$pool/.provisioning/$name.lock"
flock -n 9 || fail 'instance preparation active'
instances=$(incus list -f json)
[[ $(jq --arg name "$name" '[.[]|select(.name==$name and .status!="Stopped")]|length' <<<"$instances") == 0 ]] || fail 'instance must be stopped'
root=$pool/.mounts/$name/root
replica=$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade
view=$pool/.mounts/$name/root-view
seed_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/seed-layer
upgrade_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade-layer
container_root=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots/containers/$name/rootfs
[[ $(jq -r .root_mount "$receipt") == "$root" && $(jq -r .upgrade_mount "$receipt") == "$replica" ]] || fail 'mount pins differ'
# Remount existing members after reboot, never add/remove a member or format.
if ! findmnt -rn -M "$root" >/dev/null || ! findmnt -rn -M "$replica" >/dev/null; then
    seed=$(jq -er .seed_device "$receipt")
    [[ $seed == /dev/disk/by-uuid/"$(jq -r .seed_fsid "$receipt")" && -b $seed ]] || fail 'seed unavailable'
    # UUID aliases can resolve to an already registered RO loop view.
    seed=$(lsblk -J -o PATH,TYPE,UUID | jq -er --arg uuid "$(jq -er .seed_fsid "$receipt")" \
        '[..|objects|select(.uuid==$uuid and .type=="part")|.path]|select(length==1)|.[0]') || fail 'physical seed is not unique'
    blockdev --setro "$seed"
    seed_loop=$(losetup -j "$(realpath -e "$seed")" -O NAME --noheadings | head -n 1)
    [[ -n $seed_loop ]] || seed_loop=$(losetup --find --show --read-only "$seed")
    [[ $(blockdev --getro "$seed_loop") == 1 ]] || fail 'seed loop must be read-only'
    disk_loop=$(losetup -j "$image" -O NAME --noheadings | head -n 1)
    [[ -n $disk_loop ]] || disk_loop=$(losetup --find --show --partscan "$image")
    [[ $(blkid -p -s UUID -o value "${disk_loop}p1") == "$(jq -r .root_fsid "$receipt")" && $(blkid -p -s UUID -o value "${disk_loop}p2") == "$(jq -r .upgrade_fsid "$receipt")" ]] || fail 'filesystem pins differ'
    mkdir -p "$root" "$replica"
    findmnt -rn -M "$root" >/dev/null || mount -o "rw,subvolid=5,device=$seed_loop,device=${disk_loop}p1" "${disk_loop}p1" "$root"
    findmnt -rn -M "$replica" >/dev/null || mount -o rw,subvolid=5 "${disk_loop}p2" "$replica"
fi
assert_fs() {
    local source
    [[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$1" -o FSTYPE) == btrfs && $(findmnt -rn -M "$1" -o FSROOT) == / ]] || fail "not a top-level Btrfs mount: $1"
    source=$(findmnt -rn -M "$1" -o SOURCE)
    [[ $(blkid -p -s UUID -o value "$source") == "$2" ]] || fail "wrong filesystem: $1"
}
assert_fs "$root" "$(jq -r .root_fsid "$receipt")"
assert_fs "$replica" "$(jq -r .upgrade_fsid "$receipt")"
host_uuid=5a88e7cd-9701-40a7-8301-ef076761886c
host=$pool/.mounts/host-upgrade
[[ ! -L $host && ! -L $view ]] || fail 'unsafe mount path'
mkdir -p "$host"
findmnt -rn -M "$host" >/dev/null || mount -o rw,subvolid=5 "/dev/disk/by-uuid/$host_uuid" "$host"
assert_fs "$host" "$host_uuid"
btrfs subvolume show "$host/@" >/dev/null
[[ -z $(btrfs subvolume list -o "$host/@") ]] || fail 'nested OS subvolumes require explicit transport'
# The pair starts empty. The read-only overlay falls through to the existing
# seed-root view until a patch supplies a replacement or an OverlayFS whiteout.
state=$pool/.provisioning/$name.upgrade.json
[[ ! -L $state ]] || fail 'unsafe pair receipt'
source_snapshots=$host/.upgrade-sync/$name
received=$replica/.upgrade-sync/$name
[[ ! -L $source_snapshots && ! -L $received ]] || fail 'unsafe transport paths'
mkdir -p "$source_snapshots" "$received"
if [[ $action == pair ]]; then
    [[ ! -e $state ]] || fail 'pair exists; never repeat provisioning transfer'
    [[ -z $(find "$replica/@" -mindepth 1 -print -quit) ]] || fail 'initial upgrade must be empty'
    jq -n --arg host "$host_uuid" --arg replica "$(jq -r .upgrade_fsid "$receipt")" \
        '{phase:"pair-intent",host_fsid:$host,replica_fsid:$replica,direction:"host-to-container"}' > "$state"
else
    [[ -f $state ]] || fail 'initial pairing required'
    jq -e --arg host "$host_uuid" --arg replica "$(jq -r .upgrade_fsid "$receipt")" \
        '.phase=="paired" and .host_fsid==$host and .replica_fsid==$replica and .direction=="host-to-container"' "$state" >/dev/null || fail 'incomplete or different pairing; inspect before recovery'
fi
# Never change a lower tree under a mounted OverlayFS view. The stopped
# container's bind holds another reference, so detach that view first too.
detach_agent_mounts() {
    local target=$1 member
    for member in user soul skills shared rules memory; do
        if findmnt -rn -M "$target/agent/$member" >/dev/null; then umount "$target/agent/$member"; fi
    done
    if findmnt -rn -M "$target/opt/run-mounts/persist" >/dev/null; then umount "$target/opt/run-mounts/persist"; fi
}
if findmnt -rn -M "$container_root" >/dev/null; then
    [[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$container_root" -o FSTYPE) == overlay &&
       $(findmnt -rn -M "$container_root" -o FS-OPTIONS) == *"lowerdir=$upgrade_layer:$seed_layer"* ]] || fail 'unexpected container root mount; reconcile manually'
    detach_agent_mounts "$container_root"
    umount "$container_root"
fi
if findmnt -rn -M "$view" >/dev/null; then
    [[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$view" -o FSTYPE) == overlay &&
       $(findmnt -rn -M "$view" -o FS-OPTIONS) == *"lowerdir=$upgrade_layer:$seed_layer"* ]] || fail 'unexpected root view mount'
    detach_agent_mounts "$view"
    umount "$view"
fi
for layer in "$upgrade_layer" "$seed_layer"; do
    if findmnt -rn -M "$layer" >/dev/null; then umount "$layer"; fi
done
generation=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)-$$
parent=$(jq -r '.generation // empty' "$state")
jq --arg next "$generation" '.phase="send-intent"|.next_generation=$next' "$state" > "$state.new"
mv -T "$state.new" "$state"
sync -f "$pool/.provisioning"
btrfs subvolume snapshot -r "$host/@" "$source_snapshots/$generation"
if [[ -n $parent ]]; then
    [[ $(btrfs property get -ts "$source_snapshots/$parent" ro) == 'ro=true' && $(btrfs property get -ts "$received/$parent" ro) == 'ro=true' ]] || fail 'immutable common baseline missing'
    btrfs send -p "$source_snapshots/$parent" "$source_snapshots/$generation" | btrfs receive "$received"
else
    btrfs send "$source_snapshots/$generation" | btrfs receive "$received"
fi
sent_uuid=$(btrfs subvolume show "$source_snapshots/$generation" | awk '$1=="UUID:" {print $2}')
received_uuid=$(btrfs subvolume show "$received/$generation" | awk '$1=="Received" && $2=="UUID:" {print $3}')
[[ -n $sent_uuid && $sent_uuid == "$received_uuid" && $(btrfs property get -ts "$received/$generation" ro) == 'ro=true' ]] || fail 'receive identity/read-only receipt differs'
# Keep received snapshots immutable for future incremental sends. @ is a
# writable clone; the exposed root view, not this upgrade partition, is RO.
btrfs subvolume snapshot "$received/$generation" "$replica/.next-$generation"
mv "$replica/@" "$received/previous-$generation"
mv "$replica/.next-$generation" "$replica/@"
sync -f "$host"
sync -f "$replica"
jq --arg generation "$generation" '.phase="paired"|.generation=$generation|del(.next_generation)' "$state" > "$state.new"
mv -T "$state.new" "$state"
sync -f "$pool/.provisioning"
if [[ $action == boot ]]; then
    # Both OS layers are read-only in the guest. The upgrade partition itself
    # remains writable for receive/rotation; user siblings are separate binds.
    # Patches deleting seed files must carry whiteouts in the upgrade layer.
    instance=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$name")
    jq -e '.status=="Stopped" and .config["security.privileged"]=="false" and
        .config["security.protection.shift"]=="true" and .devices.root.pool=="identity-roots"' \
        <<<"$instance" >/dev/null || fail 'stopped identity container required for boot mounts'
    idmap=$(jq -er '.config["volatile.idmap.current"]' <<<"$instance")
    jq -e 'length==2 and all(.[]; .Hostid==1000000 and .Nsid==0 and .Maprange==1000000000) and
        any(.[]; .Isuid==true and .Isgid==false) and any(.[]; .Isgid==true and .Isuid==false)' \
        <<<"$idmap" >/dev/null || fail 'unsupported identity idmap'
    [[ -d $container_root && ! -L $container_root &&
       $(realpath -e "$container_root") == "$container_root" ]] || fail 'unsafe Incus root path'
    mkdir -p "$view" "$seed_layer" "$upgrade_layer"
    # This kernel cannot idmap an OverlayFS mount. Map its Btrfs lowers first.
    mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@" "$seed_layer"
    mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$replica/@" "$upgrade_layer"
    mount -t overlay overlay -o "ro,lowerdir=$upgrade_layer:$seed_layer" "$view"
    for member in memory rules shared skills soul user; do
        [[ -d $view/agent/$member && ! -L $view/agent/$member ]] || fail "upgrade missing /agent/$member"
        mount --bind -o X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@agent_$member" "$view/agent/$member"
        case "$member" in shared|soul) mount -o remount,bind,ro "$view/agent/$member" ;; esac
    done
    mount --bind -o X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@agent_user/persist" "$view/opt/run-mounts/persist"
    mount --rbind "$view" "$container_root"
    incus config set "$name" "volatile.last_state.idmap=$idmap"
fi
printf 'Upgrade synchronized host -> %s; user data excluded.\n' "$name"

    # remains writable for receive/rotation; user siblings are separate binds.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Provision a fresh shared root for the EXISTING configured chatbot key.
# Completed manual storage stage (no identity/backend preflight):
#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-disk 3tchedChatbot
#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --inspect-disk 3tchedChatbot
#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-container 3tchedChatbot
#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --pair-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --bind-root 3tchedChatbot
#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-adoption 3tchedChatbot
#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --sync-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
#     [--root-gib 20 --upgrade-gib 40]   # prepare-disk only
# Creates /var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool/NAME.img: raw GPT root + upgrade.
# --prepare-container defines the stopped chatbot and socket profile only;
# it does not bind the prepared root, adopt the identity or start the guest.
# This stage ends before formatting, seed attachment, Incus creation or Cozo
# registration. Existing identity mode below remains the older unpartitioned
# leaf workflow; do not pass a partitioned image to that mode.
# Usage:
#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh LABEL --session-id UUID --pubkey B64 \
#     --operator-session UUID --leaf-path ABSOLUTE_PATH --principal-group '$ROOT' \
#     [--fstorage-gib N] [--no-start]
#     [--container-name 3tchedChatbot]   # configured chatbot key only
#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh NAME --system \
#     [--image ALIAS|FINGERPRINT] [--storage POOL] [--no-start]
#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --system NAME [system options]
#
# Identity mode never signs up an account, generates/copies credentials,
# deletes/recreates a container, or attaches a leaf to an Incus filesystem.
# Clean replacement is currently scoped to the configured chatbot alias
# 3tchedChatbot. LABEL is display metadata, never authority.
# Existing native names and storage receipts are refused.
# --no-start prepares storage, reconciles and verifies attach, leaving STOPPED.
# The old native instance must be stopped. The supported owner operation
# creates a fresh parked current-schema record using the same key and SID;
# supported touch then starts it after attached readback. --no-start leaves
# the new identity parked. Credential bytes are not requested or inspected;
# supported method results redact them. This wrapper never mints credentials.
# Completion enables root/FUSE restoration on boot; --no-start records a
# stopped boot policy. Incomplete storage never receives a boot-ready marker.
# The physical seed is one immutable filesystem shared by all leaves. Storage
# preparation uses its existing seven subvolumes through a private writable
# sprout; it never snapshots, copies, sends or receives a container root.
# Each guest gets its session ID as /etc/hostname and the LXC UTS hostname.
# seed-lungs configures the persistent Incus disk attaching the identity's own
# host FUSE mount at /run/mount/3tchedFS on every start.
# The 3tched-lungs profile provides /run tmpfs and the dedicated host socket
# directory at the same /run/opdbus/lungs path inside each new container.
# Failures retain native/storage intent and private sanitized receipts.
# Host helper/catalog defaults select activated release artifacts.
# Selected overrides must be root-controlled. This is host operator maintenance,
# not a guest-accessible host socket or a new identity minting authority.
# --system remains ordinary Raccoon cloud provisioning without identity changes.
set -euo pipefail
die() { printf 'ERROR: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
need_cmd() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "missing command: $1"; }
usage() { sed -n '2,20p' "$0"; }
if [[ $# == 0 || ${1:-} == -h || ${1:-} == --help ]]; then usage; exit 0; fi
prepare_chatbot_container() (
    # Host preparation only: no identity adoption, root copy, device-add or start.
    [[ $# == 1 && $1 == 3tchedChatbot ]] || die 'usage: --prepare-container 3tchedChatbot'
    [[ $(id -u) == 0 ]] || die 'container preparation requires host root'
    for tool in incus jq findmnt stat flock realpath sync; do need_cmd "$tool"; done
    incus() { command incus --force-local "$@"; }
    umask 077
    pool_root=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool
    receipt=$pool_root/.provisioning/$1.json
    container_receipt=$pool_root/.provisioning/$1.incus.json
    [[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$pool_root" -o FSROOT) == /@3tched-leaf-pool &&
       -f $receipt && ! -L $receipt && ! -e $container_receipt && ! -L $container_receipt ]] ||
        die 'prepared disk receipt required; existing container intents must be reconciled manually'
    jq -e --arg name "$1" '.name==$name and .phase=="filesystems-prepared" and
        .layout=="raw-gpt-root-upgrade-v1" and .filesystem_prepared==true and .identity_registered==false' \
        "$receipt" >/dev/null || die 'disk is not ready for container definition'
    image=$(jq -er .image "$receipt")
    [[ $image == "$pool_root/$1.img" && -f $image && ! -L $image &&
       $(stat -c %i "$image") == "$(jq -r .image_inode "$receipt")" &&
       $(stat -c %s "$image") == "$(jq -r .image_bytes "$receipt")" ]] || die 'prepared image changed'
    exec 9>"$pool_root/.provisioning/$1.lock"
    flock -n 9 || die 'instance preparation active'
    instances=$(incus list -f json)
    jq -e --arg name "$1" 'type=="array" and all(.[]; .name!=$name)' <<<"$instances" >/dev/null ||
        die 'container already exists; never recreate it'
    [[ $(findmnt -rn -M /var/lib/incus-storage -o FSROOT) == /@incus ]] || die 'Incus subvolume not mounted'
    pool_source=/var/lib/incus-storage/identity-roots
    pools=$(incus storage list -f json)
    if jq -e 'any(.[]; .name=="identity-roots")' <<<"$pools" >/dev/null; then
        pool_json=$(incus query /1.0/storage-pools/identity-roots)
        jq -e --arg source "$pool_source" '.driver=="dir" and .status=="Created" and .config.source==$source' \
            <<<"$pool_json" >/dev/null || die 'identity-roots pool differs'
    else
        [[ ! -e /var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots &&
           ! -L /var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots &&
           ! -e $pool_source && ! -L $pool_source ]] || die 'retained pool paths require manual reconciliation'
        mkdir -m 0711 "$pool_source"
        incus storage create identity-roots dir "source=$pool_source"
    fi
    /usr/local/libexec/3tched/op-identity-root seed-profile
    sid=b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28
    public_key=[REDACTED:opaque-base64]
    jq -n --arg name "$1" --arg sid "$sid" --arg source "$pool_source" \
        '{version:1,phase:"container-create-intent",name:$name,session_id:$sid,pool_source:$source,
          identity_registered:false,root_bound:false,started:false}' > "$container_receipt"
    sync -f "$container_receipt"
    deny_policy=$(printf '%s\n' \
        'ioctl errno 1 [1,0x4008941a,SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ,0xffffffff]' \
        'ioctl errno 1 [1,0x5000940f,SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ,0xffffffff]' \
        'ioctl errno 1 [1,0x5000943f,SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ,0xffffffff]')
    incus init --empty "$1" --storage identity-roots --profile 3tched-lungs \
        --config security.privileged=false --config security.nesting=false \
        --config security.protection.shift=true --config boot.autostart=false \
        --config security.syscalls.deny_default=true --config "security.syscalls.deny=$deny_policy" \
        --config "user.opdbus.session_id=$sid" --config "user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key=$public_key" \
        --config user.display_name=control-plane-chatbot --config "raw.lxc=lxc.uts.name = $sid" </dev/null
    # Preserve the shared profile. Its historical initial.mode key is absent
    # from the sealed disk-device contract and /run already exists as 0755.
    incus config device override "$1" runtime-run
    incus config device unset "$1" runtime-run initial.mode
    instance=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$1")
    jq -e --arg name "$1" --arg sid "$sid" '.name==$name and .status=="Stopped" and
        .config["user.opdbus.session_id"]==$sid' <<<"$instance" >/dev/null || die 'stopped definition readback differs'
    jq --argjson instance "$instance" '.phase="container-defined"|.instance=$instance' \
        "$container_receipt" > "$container_receipt.new"
    sync -f "$container_receipt.new"
    mv -T "$container_receipt.new" "$container_receipt"
    sync -f "$pool_root/.provisioning"
    printf 'Stopped container defined; root binding and identity adoption remain pending.\n'
)
case $1 in
    --prepare-adoption)
        shift
        script_dir=$(dirname -- "$(realpath -e -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")
        adoption_helper=$script_dir/prepare-chatbot-adoption.sh
        [[ -x $adoption_helper ]] || adoption_helper=$script_dir/prepare-chatbot-adoption
        [[ -x $adoption_helper ]] || die 'adoption plan helper missing'
        exec "$adoption_helper" "$@"
        ;;
    --bind-root)
        shift
        script_dir=$(dirname -- "$(realpath -e -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")
        bind_helper=$script_dir/bind-instance-root.sh
        [[ -x $bind_helper ]] || bind_helper=$script_dir/bind-instance-root
        [[ -x $bind_helper ]] || die 'root binding helper missing'
        exec "$bind_helper" "$@"
        ;;
    --prepare-container)
        shift
        prepare_chatbot_container "$@"
        exit
        ;;
    --pair-upgrade|--sync-upgrade|--upgrade-boot)
        upgrade_action=pair
        [[ $1 != --sync-upgrade ]] || upgrade_action=sync
        [[ $1 != --upgrade-boot ]] || upgrade_action=boot
        shift
        script_dir=$(dirname -- "$(realpath -e -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")
        upgrade_helper=$script_dir/sync-instance-upgrade.sh
        [[ -x $upgrade_helper ]] || upgrade_helper=$script_dir/sync-instance-upgrade
        [[ -x $upgrade_helper ]] || die 'upgrade synchronization helper missing'
        exec "$upgrade_helper" "$upgrade_action" "$@"
        ;;
    --prepare-disk|--inspect-disk|--prepare-filesystems)
        disk_action=create
        [[ $1 != --inspect-disk ]] || disk_action=inspect
        [[ $1 != --prepare-filesystems ]] || disk_action=prepare
        shift
        script_dir=$(dirname -- "$(realpath -e -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")
        disk_helper=$script_dir/prepare-instance-disk.sh
        [[ -x $disk_helper ]] || disk_helper=$script_dir/prepare-instance-disk
        [[ -x $disk_helper ]] || die 'disk preparation helper is missing'
        exec "$disk_helper" "$disk_action" "$@"
        ;;
esac
SYSTEM_MODE=false SYSTEM_NAME="" ROLE=""
if [[ $1 == --system ]]; then
    SYSTEM_MODE=true; shift; SYSTEM_NAME=${1:?container name required}; shift
else ROLE=$1; shift; fi
SYSTEM_IMAGE=${SYSTEM_CONTAINER_IMAGE:-raccoon}
SYSTEM_STORAGE_POOL=${SYSTEM_STORAGE_POOL:-3tched-storage}
IMAGE=${IDENTITY_SEED_IMAGE:-3a639373bb7a} IMAGE_OVERRIDDEN=false
SYSTEM_STORAGE=$SYSTEM_STORAGE_POOL SYSTEM_STORAGE_OVERRIDDEN=false
IDENTITY_ONLY_FLAGS="" PUBKEY="" SESSION_ID="" OPERATOR_SESSION="" LEAF_PATH="" NATIVE_NAME=""
PRINCIPAL_GROUP="" FSTORAGE_GIB=2 NO_START=false
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --pubkey|--session-id|--operator-session|--leaf-path|--fstorage-gib|--container-name|--principal-group)
            option=$1; IDENTITY_ONLY_FLAGS="$IDENTITY_ONLY_FLAGS $option"
            shift; value=${1:?option requires a value}
            case "$option" in
                --pubkey) PUBKEY=$value ;; --session-id) SESSION_ID=$value ;;
                --operator-session) OPERATOR_SESSION=$value ;; --leaf-path) LEAF_PATH=$value ;;
                --fstorage-gib) FSTORAGE_GIB=$value ;; --container-name) NATIVE_NAME=$value ;;
                --principal-group) PRINCIPAL_GROUP=$value ;;
            esac ;;
        --image) shift; IMAGE=${1:?}; IMAGE_OVERRIDDEN=true ;;
        --storage) shift; SYSTEM_STORAGE=${1:?}; SYSTEM_STORAGE_OVERRIDDEN=true ;;
        --no-start) NO_START=true ;;
        --system)
            [[ $SYSTEM_MODE == false ]] || die '--system specified more than once'
            SYSTEM_MODE=true; SYSTEM_NAME=$ROLE ;;
        --identity-dir|--private-key-file|--email|--mesh-ip)
            IDENTITY_ONLY_FLAGS="$IDENTITY_ONLY_FLAGS $1"; shift; : "${1:?}"
            [[ $SYSTEM_MODE == true ]] || die 'legacy identity options are retired; use an existing authoritative session' ;;
        --ghostbridge|--semantic|--recreate)
            IDENTITY_ONLY_FLAGS="$IDENTITY_ONLY_FLAGS $1"
            [[ $SYSTEM_MODE == true ]] || die 'legacy identity options are retired; no recreate or credential/socket mounts' ;;
        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;; *) die "unknown option: $1" ;;
    esac
    shift

        'ioctl errno 1 [1,0x4008941a,SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ,0xffffffff]' \
        'ioctl errno 1 [1,0x5000940f,SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ,0xffffffff]' \
        'ioctl errno 1 [1,0x5000943f,SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ,0xffffffff]')
    incus init --empty "$1" --storage identity-roots --profile 3tched-lungs \
        --config security.privileged=false --config security.nesting=false \
        --config security.protection.shift=true --config boot.autostart=false \
        --config security.syscalls.deny_default=true --config "security.syscalls.deny=$deny_policy" \
        --config "user.opdbus.session_id=$sid" --config "user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key=$public_key" \

lungs_call() (

    # Never clear read-only receipts or treat a successful write as completion.
    printf '%s' "$args" > "$operation/call"
    [[ ! -s $operation/error ]] || { printf 'Lungs operation %s failed; inspect its protected error receipt.\n' "$method" >&2; exit 1; }
    line=$(jq -ce --arg method "$method" 'select(.plugin_id=="identity_sled" and .method==$method) | {result:{structuredContent:.result}}' "$operation/result")
    jq -ce --arg sid "$SESSION_ID" --arg name "$NATIVE_NAME" --arg key "$PUBKEY" --arg kind "$kind" '
        select(.error==null and .result.isError!=true) |
        (.result.structuredContent // ([.result.content[]? | select(.type=="text") | .text | fromjson?] | select(length==1) | .[0])) as $body |
        if $kind=="device-add" then
            ($body.result // $body) |
            select(.operation=="device_add" and (.device|type=="string" and length>0) and
                (.filesystem_uuid|type=="string" and length>0) and (.devices|type=="array")) |
            {operation,filesystem_uuid,device,devices:[.devices[]|{id,uuid,path,total_bytes,bytes_used}]}
        else $body | select(.success==true) |
        if $kind=="inventory" then
            [.. | objects | select(has("entries") and has("counts"))] | select(length==1) | .[0] |
            select(.entries|type=="array") | select(.counts|type=="object") | {verified:true}
        elif $kind=="preflight" then
            [.. | objects | select(has("wireguard_pubkey") and has("session_id") and has("expected_revision_operation_id"))] |
            select(length==1) | .[0] |             select(.session_id==$sid and .wireguard_pubkey==$key) |
            select(.expected_revision|type=="number" and .>0 and floor==.) |
            select(.expected_revision_operation_id|type=="string" and length>0) |
            {session_id,wireguard_pubkey,expected_revision,expected_revision_operation_id,previous_instance,previous_instance_etag,previous_native_instance}
        else
            (if $kind=="provision" then
                [.. | objects | select(has("committed_revision") and has("plan_sha256") and has("identity"))] |
                select(length==1) | .[0] |
                select(.plan_sha256|type=="string" and test("^[0-9a-f]{64}$")) |
                select(.operation_id|type=="string" and length>0) |
                select(.committed_revision|type=="number" and .>0 and floor==.) |
                select(.replayed|type=="boolean")
             else {identity:.} end) as $receipt |
            $receipt.identity |
            [.. | objects | select(has("wireguard_pubkey") and has("session_id"))] |
            select(length==1) | .[0] | select(.session_id==$sid and .wireguard_pubkey==$key) |
            select(.genesis|type=="string" and length>0) |
            select((.arrival_timestamp|type=="number" and .>0 and floor==.) and
                (.chain_head_at_arrival|type=="string" and length>0)) |
            select(.instance|type=="object" and .name==$name and .type=="container") |
            select($name==$sid or .principal_kind=="service") |
            select((.interface|type=="string") and ((.peer_ip==null) or (.peer_ip|type=="string"))) |
            select(.btrfs_device|type=="object") | select(.btrfs_device.cozo_id|type=="string" and length>0) |
            select(.btrfs_device | (.device_path|type=="string") and (.mount_point|type=="string") and
                (.btrfs_uuid|type=="string") and (.attached|type=="boolean")) |
            select((.active|type=="boolean") and (.mutation_index|type=="number" and .>=0 and floor==.)) |
            {session_id,principal_kind,instance:(.instance|{name,type}),interface,peer_ip,active,mutation_index,
             btrfs_device:(.btrfs_device|{device_path,mount_point,btrfs_uuid,cozo_id,attached})} as $identity |
            if $kind=="provision" then $receipt | .identity=$identity else $identity end
        end
        end' <<<"$line" >"$WORK/operation-filter.json" 2>/dev/null || {
        if [[ $kind == device-add ]]; then
            jq -r '.error.message // ([.result.content[]? | select(.type=="text") | .text] | first) // "device_add failed"' <<<"$line" >&2
        fi
        exit 1
    }
    cat "$WORK/operation-filter.json"
)

            select(.expected_revision|type=="number" and .>0 and floor==.) |
            select(.expected_revision_operation_id|type=="string" and length>0) |
            {session_id,wireguard_pubkey,expected_revision,expected_revision_operation_id,previous_instance,previous_instance_etag,previous_native_instance}
        else
            (if $kind=="provision" then
                [.. | objects | select(has("committed_revision") and has("plan_sha256") and has("identity"))] |
                select(length==1) | .[0] |
                select(.plan_sha256|type=="string" and test("^[0-9a-f]{64}$")) |
                select(.operation_id|type=="string" and length>0) |
                select(.committed_revision|type=="number" and .>0 and floor==.) |
                select(.replayed|type=="boolean")
             else {identity:.} end) as $receipt |
            $receipt.identity |
            [.. | objects | select(has("wireguard_pubkey") and has("session_id"))] |
            select(length==1) | .[0] | select(.session_id==$sid and .wireguard_pubkey==$key) |
            select(.genesis|type=="string" and length>0) |
            select((.arrival_timestamp|type=="number" and .>0 and floor==.) and
                (.chain_head_at_arrival|type=="string" and length>0)) |
            select(.instance|type=="object" and .name==$name and .type=="container") |
            select($name==$sid or .principal_kind=="service") |
            select((.interface|type=="string") and ((.peer_ip==null) or (.peer_ip|type=="string"))) |
            select(.btrfs_device|type=="object") | select(.btrfs_device.cozo_id|type=="string" and length>0) |
            select(.btrfs_device | (.device_path|type=="string") and (.mount_point|type=="string") and
                (.btrfs_uuid|type=="string") and (.attached|type=="boolean")) |
            select((.active|type=="boolean") and (.mutation_index|type=="number" and .>=0 and floor==.)) |
            {session_id,principal_kind,instance:(.instance|{name,type}),interface,peer_ip,active,mutation_index,
             btrfs_device:(.btrfs_device|{device_path,mount_point,btrfs_uuid,cozo_id,attached})} as $identity |
            if $kind=="provision" then $receipt | .identity=$identity else $identity end
        end
        end' <<<"$line" >"$WORK/operation-filter.json" 2>/dev/null || {
        if [[ $kind == device-add ]]; then
            jq -r '.error.message // ([.result.content[]? | select(.type=="text") | .text] | first) // "device_add failed"' <<<"$line" >&2

python3 - "$GRANTS_FILE" "$CHATBOT_PRINCIPAL" "$PRINCIPAL_GROUP" <<'PY'
import json, os, sys, tempfile
path, principal, group = sys.argv[1:]
with open(path) as handle:
    document = json.load(handle)
entry = document.get(principal)
if not isinstance(entry, dict):

entry["groups"] = [group]
entry.setdefault("capabilities", [])
document[principal] = entry
fd, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".capability-grants.", dir=os.path.dirname(path) or ".")
try:

# Shared physical seed and private leaves

## Manual provisioning checkpoint: partitioned instance disk

The October 11 manual workflow uses a sparse QEMU raw image under
`/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool`, mounted from `@3tched-leaf-pool` on the host's
main Btrfs pool. This subvolume isolates the storage path, but shares that
pool's capacity. The shared seed remains the separate sealed 20 GiB partition;
no instance identity or Cozo binding is written into it.

The completed image preparation step is available through the provisioner:

```sh
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-disk 3tchedChatbot
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --inspect-disk 3tchedChatbot
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-filesystems 3tchedChatbot \
  --seed-device /dev/disk/by-uuid/3415d575-7224-4484-9e0d-06854ac5f032
```

Preparation creates a 60 GiB sparse raw image with GPT: 20 GiB root and the
remaining approximately 40 GiB upgrade partition. `--root-gib` and
`--upgrade-gib` select capacities on a new image. The upgrade remainder is
slightly smaller than its requested capacity because GPT and alignment consume
space. The image and a private preparation receipt live in the leaf pool;
the receipt pins the image inode and both partition identities. An interrupted
creation retains its intent and image instead of retrying or cleaning them up.
`inspect` does not register or adopt an existing image.

The filesystem stage attaches a read-only loop view of the sealed seed and adds
the blank root partition once as its writable leaf. It inherits the seven seed
subvolumes; it does not copy the root or create replacement agent subvolumes.
Only the upgrade partition is formatted, with one `@` subvolume. Shared and soul
are read-only in the leaf; memory, rules, skills and user are writable. Private
persistence directories are ordinary directories. Both mounts stay attached for
the next manual step. The receipt records loops, mounts and fresh filesystem
UUIDs. Interrupted intents require investigation, and prepared receipts cannot
repeat device-add or formatting. Never modify the seed after leaves depend on it.

Neither stage performs seed transport, Incus creation, identity registration or
startup. They have no identity/backend preflight dependency.
Those later steps remain subject to the owner's manual
script comparison. The existing identity mode described below expects an
unpartitioned leaf and must not be used with this new partitioned image.

The upgrade lifecycle is host → container only, using Btrfs without Unison:

```sh
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --pair-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --sync-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
```

Pairing sends a read-only snapshot of host upgrade `/dev/sdc3` (`@`) to
partition 2 during provisioning, including when the first upgrade is empty.
Subsequent synchronization sends incrementally from the retained
common baseline, including deletions within the upgrade tree. Received baselines stay read-only;
the published upgrade `@` is a writable clone. Transfer intents and prior
versions are retained for recovery; interrupted publication is not retried
automatically. Snapshot retention cleanup is not implemented by this stage.

The chatbot runit startup invokes `boot` for explicitly paired storage before
starting the container. It restores existing loop/mount attachments, synchronizes,
then publishes a read-only OverlayFS OS view at `.mounts/NAME/root-view`.
The upgrade layer takes precedence over the seed-root layer; an empty upgrade
uses the installed seed. Patches removing seed files must include OverlayFS
whiteouts: deleting a file from the upgrade tree alone reveals its seed copy.
The Btrfs layers receive the container UID mapping before mounting OverlayFS,
because this kernel rejects mapping the merged overlay. The view is bound at
the Incus-managed `identity-roots` rootfs, preserving its pool definition.
Six agent subvolumes are separately bound into `/agent`; their existing writable
or read-only policies remain in effect, with private persistence bound separately.
User contents are never sent or received. Synchronization detaches stopped OS
views before rotating a lower layer; it never changes Btrfs membership.
This new image is not yet admitted by the older unpartitioned root-owner lifecycle;
its identity-root integration remains part of the subsequent provisioning step.

The seed has the seven sibling subvolumes and guest systemd FUSE service.
`@agent_rules/rules/rules.md` and `@agent_user/user/user.md` are initial
per-instance documents: their content is changed in each private writable leaf,
not in the sealed seed. Shared owner links expose cognitive memory, skills,
routing and plugins without granting authority or starting those features.

## Earlier unpartitioned-leaf integration

The following describes the earlier helper contract. Its device paths,
host-owned FUSE attachment and early backend gates are not the new manual
partitioned-disk workflow and still require reconciliation before automation.

Identity provisioning uses one immutable Btrfs seed on the physical partition
currently named `/dev/sdb2`. Each container has its own writable leaf. A leaf
stores that container's changes; it does not contain a copied root filesystem.
Golden preparation includes the wrapper and its helpers under `libexec/3tched`;
after release activation, the operator entrypoint is
`/usr/local/libexec/3tched/provision-workspace-subscriber`.

The seed's top-level layout is `@`, `@agent_memory`, `@agent_rules`,
`@agent_shared`, `@agent_skills`, `@agent_soul`, and `@agent_user`. Provisioning
uses these existing subvolumes in the sprout. It does not create snapshots,
send/receive root filesystems, copy seed images, or use an overlay root.
Readonly loop views reference the same physical partition bytes.

`provision-workspace-subscriber.sh` first verifies the mounted operator
3tchedFS session and sealed catalog, then calls the declared identity inventory
and provisioning preflight operations through their `call` files. It checks
the operation receipts before invoking the read-only
`op-identity-root seed-preflight`, followed by `seed-profile`, before creating
an empty Incus instance with the `3tched-lungs` profile.
The helper checks the physical seed identity, SEEDING flag and block read-only
state, and refuses a direct mount of the physical source. The wrapper holds
a per-session lock; the helper serializes seed loop setup and leaf creation.
`seed-create` adds the new private writable leaf once. Later starts mount
that existing leaf; stopping does not remove a Btrfs member. Failed starts
also retain membership. The bridge only verifies externally mounted storage;
its `attached` field describes logical attachment, not device membership.
The session hostname and private persistence are
created through the sprout, so those writes belong to the leaf. Persistence is
an ordinary mode-0700 directory at `@agent_user/persist`, bound to the guest's
`/opt/run-mounts/persist`. Provisioning creates no subvolumes at all: only the
seven inherited members are used. Agent soul,
and shared subvolumes remain protected in the guest view. Rules and user
preferences are instance-specific and writable in each private leaf.

Storage receipts identify this layout as `shared-partition-siblings-v2` and
pin its inherited subvolume identities plus the persistence directory's inode,
parent subvolume identity, sprout FSID and image metadata digest. The directory must remain on its
parent filesystem and cannot be a symlink, separate mount, or subvolume.
Older v1 receipts with an extra `@persist` subvolume and snapshot-based receipts are
rejected; this change does not silently migrate them or replace existing
container roots. Existing live persistence and older containers are neither
deleted nor converted; replacement must be prepared separately. Historical
soul reconciliation now verifies existing subvolumes and native devices only,
and fails when they are missing instead of creating them.

Before sealing a new base, `op-identity-image prepare TOP RELEASE_ID
PROVENANCE_JSON` records the archive provenance, offline package inventory,
critical file hashes and exact seven-member layout. It also prepares ordinary
mountpoint directories under `@/run/mount/3tchedFS` and `@/run/opdbus/lungs`.
The helper does not download or verify the archive signature, mount storage,
toggle SEEDING, format devices or create subvolumes. See
[image preparation](../../../deploy/workspace-image/README.md) for its input
contract. Creation fully verifies the pristine image before adding a leaf;
later checks verify the pinned metadata without rejecting legitimate private
package updates in the leaf.

FUSE runs on the host. Fresh provisioning selects a persistent Incus `disk`
device named `3tched`, exposing the session's own host FUSE mount at
`/run/mount/3tchedFS`. The seed needs an empty destination directory, not a
guest FUSE daemon. A native instance UUID pins the host source and process
receipt. An existing legacy hook receipt is verified without silently
converting its attachment mechanism. The common `/etc/3tched` directories
are a separate read-only Incus disk attachment, with links from the inherited
agent subvolumes.

The `3tched-lungs` Incus profile supplies these inherited devices:

```yaml
config: {}
devices:
  runtime-run:
    type: disk
    source: "tmpfs:"
    path: /run
    initial.mode: "0755"
  lungs-socket-dir:
    type: disk
    source: /run/opdbus/lungs
    path: /run/opdbus/lungs
    readonly: "true"
```

The bridge service creates its existing shared socket at
`/run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock`. Mounting its dedicated parent directory keeps
socket replacement visible to each guest without exposing other host runtime
files. `seed-profile` creates this exact profile if absent and rejects existing
configuration drift. Provisioning also verifies the inherited devices and
rejects local overrides. The `/run` tmpfs is mounted before its child devices;
image directories alone would not establish that boot ordering.

The bridge creates a root-owned socket with mode 0666 beneath the root-owned
0755 directory. Connection permission allows negotiation; each operation still
requires an authenticated identity and its existing capability grant. Host
`Bind(session)` requires UID 0 in the bridge's own user and PID namespaces.
Guest `BindCurrentContainer()` takes no session argument: it pins the socket's
original process with SO_PEERPIDFD and derives identity from the exact running
native container. Process, native UUID and authoritative identity are checked
again for each call. No SID1 file is installed in the guest.

Clean replacement is scoped to the configured chatbot key and service identity
`b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`, using the provisioner's configured native
alias `3tchedCtlbot`. Hostname remains the session UUID. The old native instance
must be stopped or authoritatively absent, and the new name and leaf must be
unused. Explicit retirement uses `identity_sled.delete_provision_record` through
the operator's mounted namespace, with the existing human write capability
and exact revision. This removes the current row and retains an audit tombstone;
startup respects that tombstone. A version3 plan permits fresh provisioning
from that exact deletion receipt. Ordinary missing rows are not accepted.
After host storage/mount
preparation, the wrapper submits a digest-pinned private plan through the
supported `identity_sled.provision_container` operation. The owner atomically
creates fresh current-schema state and binds it to the new native instance;
legacy persistence and record fields are not imported. Existing external
capability policy remains in force. Normal provisioning starts through
`touch_session`; `--no-start` leaves the fresh identity parked. Only verified
completion receives a boot-ready marker.

If creation fails, `op-identity-root seed-inspect NAME` reports sanitized
receipt metadata and recovery guidance without mounting, formatting or
retrying device-add. Preserve the receipt, base, leaf and mappings until the
recorded intent and actual membership have been reconciled.

Preparing or changing the live seed is a separate operator action. The helper
does not set or clear SEEDING, format the partition, or unmount an unrelated
source mount. Once leaves depend on a seed, that seed must remain unchanged.
At boot, the host storage service uses `seed-readonly` to verify the physical
partition identity and existing SEEDING state, then restore its volatile block
read-only flag before restoring opted-in roots. This never changes filesystem
membership or the SEEDING flag.
The current source change has not been deployed or validated with concurrent
live containers on the fresh base. The September 30 file-backed and physical
seed experiments did demonstrate independent writes, peer-active remounts and
cold loop recreation using distinct read-only views of the same seed on this
kernel. That evidence does not validate this new image/layout or a full host
reboot. There is no fallback to copied seeds if a kernel rejects the shared
arrangement. The owner's current sequencing instruction defers all tests until
after deployment; a successful build alone is not a workflow validation.

# Shared physical seed and private leaves

## Manual provisioning checkpoint: partitioned instance disk

The October 11 manual workflow uses a sparse QEMU raw image under
`/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool`, mounted from `@3tched-leaf-pool` on the host's
main Btrfs pool. This subvolume isolates the storage path, but shares that
pool's capacity. The shared seed remains the separate sealed 20 GiB partition;
no instance identity or Cozo binding is written into it.

The completed image preparation step is available through the provisioner:

```sh
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-disk 3tchedChatbot
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --inspect-disk 3tchedChatbot
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-filesystems 3tchedChatbot \
  --seed-device /dev/disk/by-uuid/3415d575-7224-4484-9e0d-06854ac5f032
```

Preparation creates a 60 GiB sparse raw image with GPT: 20 GiB root and the
remaining approximately 40 GiB upgrade partition. `--root-gib` and
`--upgrade-gib` select capacities on a new image. The upgrade remainder is
slightly smaller than its requested capacity because GPT and alignment consume
space. The image and a private preparation receipt live in the leaf pool;
the receipt pins the image inode and both partition identities. An interrupted
creation retains its intent and image instead of retrying or cleaning them up.
`inspect` does not register or adopt an existing image.

The filesystem stage attaches a read-only loop view of the sealed seed and adds
the blank root partition once as its writable leaf. It inherits the seven seed
subvolumes; it does not copy the root or create replacement agent subvolumes.
Only the upgrade partition is formatted, with one `@` subvolume. Shared and soul
are read-only in the leaf; memory, rules, skills and user are writable. Private
persistence directories are ordinary directories. Both mounts stay attached for
the next manual step. The receipt records loops, mounts and fresh filesystem
UUIDs. Interrupted intents require investigation, and prepared receipts cannot
repeat device-add or formatting. Never modify the seed after leaves depend on it.

Neither stage performs seed transport, Incus creation, identity registration or
startup. They have no identity/backend preflight dependency.
Those later steps remain subject to the owner's manual
script comparison. The existing identity mode described below expects an
unpartitioned leaf and must not be used with this new partitioned image.

The upgrade lifecycle is host → container only, using Btrfs without Unison:

```sh
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --pair-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --sync-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
```

Pairing sends a read-only snapshot of host upgrade `/dev/sdc3` (`@`) to
partition 2 during provisioning, including when the first upgrade is empty.
Subsequent synchronization sends incrementally from the retained
common baseline, including deletions within the upgrade tree. Received baselines stay read-only;
the published upgrade `@` is a writable clone. Transfer intents and prior
versions are retained for recovery; interrupted publication is not retried
automatically. Snapshot retention cleanup is not implemented by this stage.

The chatbot runit startup invokes `boot` for explicitly paired storage before
starting the container. It restores existing loop/mount attachments, synchronizes,
then publishes a read-only OverlayFS OS view at `.mounts/NAME/root-view`.
The upgrade layer takes precedence over the seed-root layer; an empty upgrade
uses the installed seed. Patches removing seed files must include OverlayFS
whiteouts: deleting a file from the upgrade tree alone reveals its seed copy.
The Btrfs layers receive the container UID mapping before mounting OverlayFS,
because this kernel rejects mapping the merged overlay. The view is bound at
the Incus-managed `identity-roots` rootfs, preserving its pool definition.
Six agent subvolumes are separately bound into `/agent`; their existing writable
or read-only policies remain in effect, with private persistence bound separately.
User contents are never sent or received. Synchronization detaches stopped OS
views before rotating a lower layer; it never changes Btrfs membership.
This new image is not yet admitted by the older unpartitioned root-owner lifecycle;
its identity-root integration remains part of the subsequent provisioning step.

The seed has the seven sibling subvolumes and guest systemd FUSE service.
`@agent_rules/rules/rules.md` and `@agent_user/user/user.md` are initial
per-instance documents: their content is changed in each private writable leaf,
not in the sealed seed. Shared owner links expose cognitive memory, skills,
routing and plugins without granting authority or starting those features.

## Earlier unpartitioned-leaf integration

The following describes the earlier helper contract. Its device paths,
host-owned FUSE attachment and early backend gates are not the new manual
partitioned-disk workflow and still require reconciliation before automation.

Identity provisioning uses one immutable Btrfs seed on the physical partition
currently named `/dev/sdb2`. Each container has its own writable leaf. A leaf
stores that container's changes; it does not contain a copied root filesystem.
Golden preparation includes the wrapper and its helpers under `libexec/3tched`;
after release activation, the operator entrypoint is
`/usr/local/libexec/3tched/provision-workspace-subscriber`.

The seed's top-level layout is `@`, `@agent_memory`, `@agent_rules`,
`@agent_shared`, `@agent_skills`, `@agent_soul`, and `@agent_user`. Provisioning
uses these existing subvolumes in the sprout. It does not create snapshots,
send/receive root filesystems, copy seed images, or use an overlay root.
Readonly loop views reference the same physical partition bytes.

`provision-workspace-subscriber.sh` first verifies the mounted operator
3tchedFS session and sealed catalog, then calls the declared identity inventory
and provisioning preflight operations through their `call` files. It checks
the operation receipts before invoking the read-only
`op-identity-root seed-preflight`, followed by `seed-profile`, before creating
an empty Incus instance with the `3tched-lungs` profile.
The helper checks the physical seed identity, SEEDING flag and block read-only
state, and refuses a direct mount of the physical source. The wrapper holds
a per-session lock; the helper serializes seed loop setup and leaf creation.
`seed-create` adds the new private writable leaf once. Later starts mount
that existing leaf; stopping does not remove a Btrfs member. Failed starts
also retain membership. The bridge only verifies externally mounted storage;
its `attached` field describes logical attachment, not device membership.
The session hostname and private persistence are
created through the sprout, so those writes belong to the leaf. Persistence is
an ordinary mode-0700 directory at `@agent_user/persist`, bound to the guest's
`/opt/run-mounts/persist`. Provisioning creates no subvolumes at all: only the
seven inherited members are used. Agent soul,
and shared subvolumes remain protected in the guest view. Rules and user
preferences are instance-specific and writable in each private leaf.

Storage receipts identify this layout as `shared-partition-siblings-v2` and
pin its inherited subvolume identities plus the persistence directory's inode,
parent subvolume identity, sprout FSID and image metadata digest. The directory must remain on its
parent filesystem and cannot be a symlink, separate mount, or subvolume.
Older v1 receipts with an extra `@persist` subvolume and snapshot-based receipts are
rejected; this change does not silently migrate them or replace existing
container roots. Existing live persistence and older containers are neither
deleted nor converted; replacement must be prepared separately. Historical
soul reconciliation now verifies existing subvolumes and native devices only,
and fails when they are missing instead of creating them.

Before sealing a new base, `op-identity-image prepare TOP RELEASE_ID
PROVENANCE_JSON` records the archive provenance, offline package inventory,
critical file hashes and exact seven-member layout. It also prepares ordinary
mountpoint directories under `@/run/mount/3tchedFS` and `@/run/opdbus/lungs`.
The helper does not download or verify the archive signature, mount storage,
toggle SEEDING, format devices or create subvolumes. See
[image preparation](../../../deploy/workspace-image/README.md) for its input
contract. Creation fully verifies the pristine image before adding a leaf;
later checks verify the pinned metadata without rejecting legitimate private
package updates in the leaf.

FUSE runs on the host. Fresh provisioning selects a persistent Incus `disk`
device named `3tched`, exposing the session's own host FUSE mount at
`/run/mount/3tchedFS`. The seed needs an empty destination directory, not a
guest FUSE daemon. A native instance UUID pins the host source and process
receipt. An existing legacy hook receipt is verified without silently
converting its attachment mechanism. The common `/etc/3tched` directories
are a separate read-only Incus disk attachment, with links from the inherited
agent subvolumes.

The `3tched-lungs` Incus profile supplies these inherited devices:

```yaml
config: {}
devices:
  runtime-run:
    type: disk
    source: "tmpfs:"
    path: /run
    initial.mode: "0755"
  lungs-socket-dir:
    type: disk
    source: /run/opdbus/lungs
    path: /run/opdbus/lungs
    readonly: "true"
```

The bridge service creates its existing shared socket at
`/run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock`. Mounting its dedicated parent directory keeps
socket replacement visible to each guest without exposing other host runtime
files. `seed-profile` creates this exact profile if absent and rejects existing
configuration drift. Provisioning also verifies the inherited devices and
rejects local overrides. The `/run` tmpfs is mounted before its child devices;
image directories alone would not establish that boot ordering.

The bridge creates a root-owned socket with mode 0666 beneath the root-owned
0755 directory. Connection permission allows negotiation; each operation still
requires an authenticated identity and its existing capability grant. Host
`Bind(session)` requires UID 0 in the bridge's own user and PID namespaces.
Guest `BindCurrentContainer()` takes no session argument: it pins the socket's
original process with SO_PEERPIDFD and derives identity from the exact running
native container. Process, native UUID and authoritative identity are checked
again for each call. No SID1 file is installed in the guest.

Clean replacement is scoped to the configured chatbot key and service identity
`b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`, using the provisioner's configured native
alias `3tchedCtlbot`. Hostname remains the session UUID. The old native instance
must be stopped or authoritatively absent, and the new name and leaf must be
unused. Explicit retirement uses `identity_sled.delete_provision_record` through
the operator's mounted namespace, with the existing human write capability
and exact revision. This removes the current row and retains an audit tombstone;
startup respects that tombstone. A version3 plan permits fresh provisioning
from that exact deletion receipt. Ordinary missing rows are not accepted.
After host storage/mount
preparation, the wrapper submits a digest-pinned private plan through the
supported `identity_sled.provision_container` operation. The owner atomically
creates fresh current-schema state and binds it to the new native instance;
legacy persistence and record fields are not imported. Existing external
capability policy remains in force. Normal provisioning starts through
`touch_session`; `--no-start` leaves the fresh identity parked. Only verified
completion receives a boot-ready marker.

If creation fails, `op-identity-root seed-inspect NAME` reports sanitized
receipt metadata and recovery guidance without mounting, formatting or
retrying device-add. Preserve the receipt, base, leaf and mappings until the
recorded intent and actual membership have been reconciled.

Preparing or changing the live seed is a separate operator action. The helper
does not set or clear SEEDING, format the partition, or unmount an unrelated
source mount. Once leaves depend on a seed, that seed must remain unchanged.
At boot, the host storage service uses `seed-readonly` to verify the physical
partition identity and existing SEEDING state, then restore its volatile block
read-only flag before restoring opted-in roots. This never changes filesystem
membership or the SEEDING flag.
The current source change has not been deployed or validated with concurrent
live containers on the fresh base. The September 30 file-backed and physical
seed experiments did demonstrate independent writes, peer-active remounts and
cold loop recreation using distinct read-only views of the same seed on this
kernel. That evidence does not validate this new image/layout or a full host
reboot. There is no fallback to copied seeds if a kernel rejects the shared
arrangement. The owner's current sequencing instruction defers all tests until
after deployment; a successful build alone is not a workflow validation.

See the [Btrfs seeding documentation](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Seeding-device.html).

#!/bin/sh
# Host storage owner: remount/receive existing GPT members, never mint/start.
set -eu
pool=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool
receipt=$pool/.provisioning/3tchedChatbot.boot.json
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ]
[ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSROOT)" = /@3tched-leaf-pool ]
[ -f "$receipt" ] && [ ! -L "$receipt" ]
[ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a "$receipt")" = 0:0:600 ]
jq -e '.version==1 and .name=="3tchedChatbot" and
    .session_id=="b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28" and
    .identity_registered==true and .restore_existing_pair==true' "$receipt" >/dev/null
state=$(incus --force-local query /1.0/instances/3tchedChatbot/state | jq -er .status)
root=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots/containers/3tchedChatbot/rootfs
case "$state" in
    Stopped) /usr/local/libexec/3tched/sync-instance-upgrade boot 3tchedChatbot ;;
    Running)
        # A service restart must not replace a running container's lowers.
        [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o FSTYPE)" = overlay ]
        case ",$(findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o OPTIONS)," in *,ro,*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
        ;;
    *) echo "unsupported chatbot state: $state" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

#!/bin/sh
# Mount physical-seed roots after Incus API readiness, then start only ready
# session instances (including the fixed chatbot alias). Staging names remain
# stopped. This is storage
# readiness, without a bridge/lungs dependency. A service restart observes
# running instances without stopping them; finish never detaches their roots.
exec 2>&1
rm -f /run/opdbus/runit-ready/identity-roots

wait_dep() {
    sv start "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    i=0
    until sv check "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
        i=$((i + 1))
        [ "$i" -ge 90 ] && { echo "dependency $1 not ready after 90s" >&2; exit 1; }
        sleep 1
    done
}

wait_dep incusd

i=0
until incus info >/dev/null 2>&1; do
    i=$((i + 1))
    if [ "$i" -ge 60 ]; then
        echo "incusd API not ready" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 1
done

helper=/usr/local/libexec/3tched/op-identity-root
gpt=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool/.provisioning/3tchedChatbot.boot.json
if [ -e "$gpt" ] || [ -L "$gpt" ]; then
    /usr/local/libexec/3tched/restore-chatbot-root || exit 1
    /usr/local/libexec/3tched/runit-ready-signal identity-roots
    exec pause
fi
physical=${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_STATE:-/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/seed-identities}
legacy=${IDENTITIES:-/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/identities}
physical_present=0
seed_readonly_ready=0
failed=0
for receipt in "$physical"/*/state.json; do
    [ -e "$receipt" ] || [ -L "$receipt" ] || continue
    physical_present=1
    name=$(basename "$(dirname "$receipt")")
    if [ "$name" != 3tchedChatbot ] && ! printf '%s' "$name" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'; then
        echo "physical seed staging receipt $name: boot disabled"
        continue
    fi
    marker="$physical/$name/boot-ready.json"
    if [ ! -e "$marker" ] && [ ! -L "$marker" ]; then
        echo "physical seed $name: no authoritative-completion boot opt-in; skipped"
        continue
    fi
    # A canonical name alone does not prove provisioning completed. The helper
    # checks the owner attestation marker and all storage/native identity pins.
    if ! jq -e --arg name "$name" '
        .name == $name and .phase == "ready" and
        (.session == $name or ($name == "3tchedChatbot" and .session == "b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28"))
    ' "$receipt" >/dev/null; then
        echo "physical seed $name: invalid/incomplete receipt; legacy suppressed" >&2
        failed=$((failed + 1))
        continue
    fi
    start_on_boot=$(jq -er '.start_on_boot | select(type == "boolean") | tostring' "$marker") || {
        echo "physical seed $name: invalid boot completion policy" >&2
        failed=$((failed + 1))
        continue
    }
    # The physical partition's kernel RO flag is volatile across reboot.
    # The host owner restores it once, after ready/opt-in selection and before
    # any seed-check/up; verification failures stop boot restoration closed.
    if [ "$seed_readonly_ready" -eq 0 ]; then
        "$helper" seed-readonly || { echo "physical seed read-only enforcement failed" >&2; exit 1; }
        seed_readonly_ready=1
    fi
    state=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$name/state" | jq -er '.status') || state=unknown
    case "$state" in
        Running)
            if "$helper" seed-check "$name"; then
                "$helper" seed-lungs "$name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
            ;;
        Stopped)
            if "$helper" seed-up "$name" && "$helper" seed-lungs "$name"; then
                if [ "$start_on_boot" = true ]; then incus start "$name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
                else echo "physical seed $name: storage restored; boot start disabled"; fi
            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
            ;;
        *) echo "physical seed $name: unsupported native status $state" >&2
            failed=$((failed + 1)) ;;
    esac
done
if [ "$physical_present" -eq 1 ]; then
    # A direct legacy lower mount conflicts with sprouts from the SAME seed,
    # even for a different identity. Do not invoke legacy `up` in this mode.
    for image in "$legacy"/*/identity.img; do
        [ -f "$image" ] || continue
        name=$(basename "$(dirname "$image")")
        if [ -e "$physical/$name/state.json" ] || [ -L "$physical/$name/state.json" ]; then
            echo "legacy identity $name: suppressed by physical seed receipt"
        else
            echo "legacy identity $name: migration or independent lower required; shared seed direct mount suppressed" >&2
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        fi
    done
else
    "$helper" up || failed=$((failed + 1))
    "$helper" status || failed=$((failed + 1))
fi
[ "$failed" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$failed identity root startup check(s) failed" >&2; exit 1; }
/usr/local/libexec/3tched/runit-ready-signal identity-roots
exec pause

        continue

        continue

    # checks the owner attestation marker and all storage/native identity pins.
    if ! jq -e --arg name "$name" '

        (.session == $name or ($name == "3tchedChatbot" and .session == "b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28"))

        continue

            if "$helper" seed-check "$name"; then

            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
            ;;
        Stopped)
            if "$helper" seed-up "$name" && "$helper" seed-lungs "$name"; then
                if [ "$start_on_boot" = true ]; then incus start "$name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
                else echo "physical seed $name: storage restored; boot start disabled"; fi
            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
            ;;

    # A direct legacy lower mount conflicts with sprouts from the SAME seed,

            echo "legacy identity $name: suppressed by physical seed receipt"
        else
            echo "legacy identity $name: migration or independent lower required; shared seed direct mount suppressed" >&2
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        fi
    done
else
    "$helper" up || failed=$((failed + 1))
    "$helper" status || failed=$((failed + 1))
fi
[ "$failed" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$failed identity root startup check(s) failed" >&2; exit 1; }
/usr/local/libexec/3tched/runit-ready-signal identity-roots
exec pause

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Host maintenance: attach existing shared empty/default folders. No content,
# credentials, storage membership, or container start is changed here.
set -euo pipefail
die() { printf 'workspace folders: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ $# == 1 && $1 =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,62}$ ]] || die 'usage: CONTAINER'
container=$1
[[ $(id -u) == 0 ]] || die 'requires host root'
safe_host_directory() {
    local path=$1 mode
    [[ -d $path && $(realpath -e -- "$path") == "$path" ]] || die 'host directory must exist at its canonical path'
    while :; do
        [[ ! -L $path && $(stat -c %u -- "$path") == 0 ]] || die 'host path must be root-owned without symlinks'
        mode=$(stat -c %a -- "$path")
        (( (8#$mode & 022) == 0 )) || die 'host path must not be writable by group or others'
        [[ $path == / ]] && break
        path=$(dirname -- "$path")
    done
}
for directory in /etc/3tched /etc/3tched/skills /etc/3tched/rules /etc/3tched/user /etc/3tched/shared /etc/3tched/soul /etc/3tched/memory; do
    safe_host_directory "$directory"
done
expected='{"type":"disk","source":"/etc/3tched","path":"/etc/3tched","readonly":"true","shift":"true"}'
observe() {
    native=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$container")
    printf '%s\n' "$native" | jq -e --arg name "$container" --argjson expected "$expected" '
        .name==$name and .type=="container" and .status=="Stopped" and
        (.expanded_config["security.privileged"] // "false")=="false" and
        (.expanded_devices | type)=="object" and
        .devices.root.type=="disk" and .devices.root.path=="/" and
        .devices.root==.expanded_devices.root and
        all(.expanded_devices[]; .path | type=="string" and (explode | all(.>=32 and .!=127))) and
        ((.devices["3tched-config"]==null and .expanded_devices["3tched-config"]==null) or
         (.devices["3tched-config"]==$expected and .expanded_devices["3tched-config"]==$expected)) and
        all(.expanded_devices | to_entries[];
            .value.type=="disk" and
            (.key=="root" or .key=="3tched-config" or
             (.value.path | type=="string" and .!="/" and .!="/etc" and
              .!="/etc/3tched" and (startswith("/etc/3tched/") | not))))
    ' >/dev/null || die 'container must be stopped/unprivileged with no conflicting or inherited config mount'
    # Reject lexical aliases that could bypass overlap checks (e.g. /etc/./).
    while IFS= read -r target; do
        [[ $target == /* && $(realpath -ms -- "$target") == "$target" ]] || die 'native disk target is not canonical'
    done < <(printf '%s\n' "$native" | jq -r '.expanded_devices[] | .path')
}
observe
native_uuid=$(printf '%s\n' "$native" | jq -er '.config["volatile.uuid"] | select(type=="string" and length>0)')
if printf '%s\n' "$native" | jq -e '.devices["3tched-config"]==null' >/dev/null; then
    incus config device add "$container" 3tched-config disk \
        source=/etc/3tched path=/etc/3tched readonly=true shift=true
fi
observe
printf '%s\n' "$native" | jq -e --arg uuid "$native_uuid" --argjson expected "$expected" '
    .config["volatile.uuid"]==$uuid and .devices["3tched-config"]==$expected and
    .expanded_devices["3tched-config"]==$expected
' >/dev/null || die 'native config attachment readback changed or failed'
printf 'Verified read-only host workspace folders for %s; container remains stopped.\n' "$container"

#!/bin/sh
# op-identity-root — bring identities up from their own devices (OD-86).
# Installed by the release at /usr/local/libexec/3tched/op-identity-root and
# run at boot by the identity-roots runit service after incusd.
#
# Legacy commands use identity.img plus overlay roots. Explicit seed-* commands
# instead use one shared physical SEED partition with a private writable leaf;
# their root-only descriptors are storage receipts, never identity authority.
# Legacy roots use /var/lib/opdbus-runtime/identities/<session>/identity.img
# holding a btrfs filesystem labelled identity-<session>. For each this script
#
#   1) attaches and mounts the device at <identity>/device,
#   2) mounts the container root as overlay(Raccoon, device/upper),
#   3) mounts the identity's lungs (3tchedFS with a call file per method),
#   4) starts the Incus container named <session>.
#
# The shared lower layer is the read-only Raccoon partition, shown through an
# idmapped view so Incus never shifts (chowns) the root into the upper layer.
# A failure stays inside that identity: the script logs it and moves on, and
# it never gates incusd or any service container.
#
# Usage:
#   sudo op-identity-root up [<session>...]     # default: every identity
#   sudo op-identity-root down <session>...
#   sudo op-identity-root status
#   sudo ARCHIVE_EXISTING=1 op-identity-root create <session> [size]
#                                  # give an existing identity a device, fresh on Raccoon
#   sudo op-identity-root seed-create NAME SESSION_UUID LEAF_PATH SIZE_BYTES
#   sudo op-identity-root seed-preflight # read-only source/helper readiness
#   sudo op-identity-root seed-profile # prepare exact shared lungs Incus profile
#   sudo op-identity-root seed-inspect NAME # read-only retained receipt/guidance
#   sudo op-identity-root seed-up NAME   # mount only; deliberately start separately
#   sudo op-identity-root seed-down NAME # stopped candidate required; retain leaf
#   sudo op-identity-root seed-rename OLD SESSION_UUID # after seed-down and Incus rename
#   sudo op-identity-root seed-check NAME # observe mounted root, including Running
#   sudo op-identity-root seed-lungs NAME # host-private mount; verify only if Running
#   sudo op-identity-root seed-enable-boot NAME [true|false] # AFTER authoritative attach/Get proof
#
# Environment overrides (defaults shown):
#   RACCOON_UUID=b6561d54-3c69-4897-a2f3-79b867e33601
#   SEEDS=/var/lib/opdbus-seeds            read-only Raccoon mount (fstab)
#   SEEDS_IDMAP=/var/lib/opdbus-seeds-idmap
#   IDMAP='b:0:1000000:1000000000'         must match the containers' idmap
#   IDENTITIES=/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/identities
#   POOL=identity-roots                    Incus dir pool for identity roots
#   LUNGS_RUN=/run/opdbus-lungs
#   LUNGS_SOCKET=/run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock    the bridge's shared lungs socket
#   THREETCHED_FS=/usr/local/bin/threetched-fs    the release binary
#   OP_IDENTITY_IMAGE_HELPER=/usr/local/libexec/3tched/op-identity-image
set -u

RACCOON_UUID=${RACCOON_UUID:-b6561d54-3c69-4897-a2f3-79b867e33601}
SEEDS=${SEEDS:-/var/lib/opdbus-seeds}
SEEDS_IDMAP=${SEEDS_IDMAP:-/var/lib/opdbus-seeds-idmap}
IDMAP=${IDMAP:-b:0:1000000:1000000000}
IDENTITIES=${IDENTITIES:-/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/identities}
POOL=${POOL:-identity-roots}
POOL_PATH=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/$POOL/containers
LUNGS_RUN=${LUNGS_RUN:-/run/opdbus-lungs}
LUNGS_SOCKET=${LUNGS_SOCKET:-/run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock}
THREETCHED_FS=${THREETCHED_FS:-/usr/local/bin/threetched-fs}
STATE=/dev/shm/opdbus/state
CATALOG=/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs

log() { printf '%s\n' "op-identity-root: $*" >&2; }

# Session ids are container names; accept only the canonical UUID shape so a
# directory name can never smuggle a path or an option into a command.
valid_session() {
    printf '%s' "$1" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'
}

validate_seed_defaults() {
    binary=$SEEDS_IDMAP/usr/local/bin/threetched-fs
    agents=$SEEDS_IDMAP/agent/rules/AGENTS.md
    [ -f "$binary" ] && [ ! -L "$binary" ] && [ -x "$binary" ] || {
        log "identity seed 3tchedFS binary is missing or not a regular executable: $binary"
        return 1
    }
    [ -f "$agents" ] && [ ! -L "$agents" ] || {
        log "identity seed agent defaults are missing or not a regular file: $agents"
        return 1
    }
}

# Accept only named human/chatbot identity instances. Archived identities retain

seed_private_dir() {

seed_shared_lock() {

seed_inspect() (

    printf '%s' "$inspect_name" | grep -Eq '^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,62}$' || seed_fail "unsafe instance name"
    inspect_state=${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_STATE:-/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/seed-identities}
    inspect_receipt=$inspect_state/$inspect_name/state.json
    seed_secure_path "$inspect_receipt"
    [ -f "$inspect_receipt" ] && [ "$(stat -c %a "$inspect_receipt")" = 600 ] &&
        [ "$(stat -c %s "$inspect_receipt")" -le 16384 ] || seed_fail "unsafe inspection receipt"

        .version == 1 and .layout == "shared-partition-siblings-v2" and .name == $name and
        (.phase == "create-intent" or .phase == "device-add-intent" or .phase == "layout-intent" or .phase == "ready") and
        ([.session,.seed_fsid,.instance_uuid,.boot_id] | all(type == "string" and test("^[0-9a-f]{8}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$"))) and
        ([.leaf,.root] | all(type == "string" and startswith("/") and (test("[[:cntrl:]]") | not)))

        recovery:(if .phase == "ready" then "Preserve the exact immutable seed and leaf pair. Use seed-check for mounted verification; seed-up only for the stopped pinned instance."
        else "Retain receipt, seed, leaf and mappings. Do not retry creation, ADD_DEV, cleanup or reformat. A host operator must inspect the recorded intent and actual membership before any separately authorized recovery." end),
        verification:"Receipt metadata only; storage/native state has not been verified."}' "$inspect_receipt"

seed_empty_dir() {

seed_super() {
    ss=$(btrfs inspect-internal dump-super "$1")
    printf '%s\n' "$ss" | awk '$1 == "fsid" {print $2; exit}'
}
seed_verify_source() {
    seed_device=$(readlink -f -- "${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_DEVICE:-/dev/disk/by-partuuid/${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_PARTUUID:-911b270a-a88f-48cd-bf9c-9dcac4cdefe8}}")
    [ -b "$seed_device" ] || seed_fail "seed is not a block device"
    [ "$(blockdev --getro "$seed_device")" = 1 ] || seed_fail "physical seed block device is not enforced read-only"
    seed_verify_source_identity

seed_verify_source_identity() {
    # Duplicate seed FSIDs make by-uuid aliases ambiguous once views exist.
    # The physical partition ID stays distinct from every loop view.
    seed_partuuid=${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_PARTUUID:-911b270a-a88f-48cd-bf9c-9dcac4cdefe8}
    seed_device=$(readlink -f -- "${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_DEVICE:-/dev/disk/by-partuuid/$seed_partuuid}")
    [ -b "$seed_device" ] || seed_fail "seed is not a block device"
    seed_secure_path "$(dirname -- "$seed_device")"
    [ "$(stat -c %u "$seed_device")" = 0 ] &&
        [ $((0$(stat -c %a "$seed_device") & 002)) -eq 0 ] || seed_fail "unsafe block device ownership or mode"
    super=$(btrfs inspect-internal dump-super "$seed_device")
    printf '%s\n' "$super" | grep -q 'SEEDING' || seed_fail "partition is not already a true Btrfs seed"
    source_fsid=$(printf '%s\n' "$super" | awk '$1 == "fsid" {print $2; exit}')
    source_generation=$(printf '%s\n' "$super" | awk '$1 == "generation" {print $2; exit}')
    valid_session "$source_fsid" || seed_fail "invalid seed FSID"
    [ -n "$source_generation" ] || seed_fail "absent seed generation"
    expected_seed_fsid=${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_EXPECTED_UUID:-$RACCOON_UUID}
    valid_session "$expected_seed_fsid" && [ "$source_fsid" = "$expected_seed_fsid" ] || seed_fail "seed differs from expected UUID"
    [ -z "${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_DEVICE:-}" ] || [ -n "${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_EXPECTED_UUID:-}" ] || seed_fail "explicit seed device requires explicit expected UUID"
    if [ -z "${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_DEVICE:-}" ]; then
        devno=$(stat -c '%t:%T' "$seed_device")
        major=${devno%:*} minor=${devno#*:}
        [ -f "/sys/dev/block/$((0x$major)):$((0x$minor))/partition" ] &&
            [ "$source_fsid" = "$expected_seed_fsid" ] || seed_fail "default source is not the expected physical seed partition"

seed_readonly() (
    # Host mount-owner maintenance: only restore the volatile kernel RO flag.
    # Never convert a filesystem to SEEDING or alter any mount/member/leaf.
    set -eu
    umask 077
    [ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || seed_fail "operator seed-readonly requires root"
    seed_shared_lock
    seed_verify_source_identity
    valid_session "$seed_partuuid" || seed_fail "invalid physical seed PARTUUID"
    [ "$(readlink -f -- "/dev/disk/by-partuuid/$seed_partuuid")" = "$seed_device" ] ||
        seed_fail "seed-readonly requires the expected physical PARTUUID"
    devno=$(stat -c '%t:%T' "$seed_device")
    major=${devno%:*} minor=${devno#*:}
    [ -f "/sys/dev/block/$((0x$major)):$((0x$minor))/partition" ] ||
        seed_fail "seed-readonly requires a physical partition"
    case "$(readlink -f -- "/sys/dev/block/$((0x$major)):$((0x$minor))")" in
        /sys/devices/virtual/*) seed_fail "seed-readonly refuses a virtual partition" ;;
        /sys/devices/*) ;;
        *) seed_fail "seed-readonly cannot verify the physical device path" ;;
    esac
    readonly_fsid=$source_fsid readonly_generation=$source_generation
    blockdev --setro "$seed_device" || seed_fail "cannot enforce physical seed read-only"
    seed_verify_source
    [ "$source_fsid" = "$readonly_fsid" ] && [ "$source_generation" = "$readonly_generation" ] ||
        seed_fail "seed changed while enforcing read-only"

)
seed_no_direct_mount() {
    # Resolve source aliases to block rdev; do not confuse distinct loop views

    for mounted_source in $(findmnt -rn -o SOURCE); do
        mounted_source=${mounted_source%%\[*}
        case "$mounted_source" in /*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
        resolved_source=$(readlink -f -- "$mounted_source") || continue
        [ -b "$resolved_source" ] || continue
        [ "$(stat -c '%t:%T' "$resolved_source")" != "$(stat -c '%t:%T' "$seed_device")" ] ||
            seed_fail "directly mounted seed source; unmount it and keep its fstab entry noauto"
    done

seed_preflight() (
