#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
IFS=$'\n\t'

LAYOUT=shared-partition-siblings-v2
SCHEMA_VERSION=1
IMAGE_REL=@/usr/share/op-dbus/image
MEMBERS=$'@\n@agent_memory\n@agent_rules\n@agent_shared\n@agent_skills\n@agent_soul\n@agent_user'
ARTIFACTS=(release.json provenance.json layout.json packages.tsv components.tsv critical-files.json critical-files.sha256 maintenance.txt)
CRITICAL_PATHS=(etc/os-release etc/fstab usr/lib/systemd/systemd usr/sbin/init)
REQUIRED_COMPONENTS=(base-files dpkg systemd systemd-sysv)

fail() { printf 'op-identity-image: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
usage() {
    cat >&2 <<'EOF'
Usage:
  op-identity-image prepare TOP RELEASE_ID PROVENANCE_JSON
  op-identity-image verify TOP
  op-identity-image verify-metadata TOP
  op-identity-image inspect TOP

TOP is an already mounted Btrfs top-level directory containing exactly the
seven shared workspace sibling subvolumes. prepare writes image metadata and
two runtime mountpoint directories inside @; it never mounts, formats, changes
seeding state, copies a root tree, or creates a subvolume.
EOF
    exit 2
}

canonical_top() {
    local input=$1 resolved
    [[ -d $input && ! -L $input ]] || fail "TOP must be an existing ordinary directory: $input"
    resolved=$(realpath -e -- "$input") || fail "cannot resolve TOP"
    [[ $resolved == "$input" && $resolved != / ]] || fail "TOP must be an absolute canonical path other than /"
    TOP=$resolved
    GUEST=$TOP/@
    [[ -d $GUEST && ! -L $GUEST ]] || fail "TOP/@ must be an ordinary guest root directory"
}

safe_dir_chain() {
    local rel=$1 path=$TOP component
    IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<< "$rel"
    for component in "${parts[@]}"; do
        path=$path/$component
        [[ -d $path && ! -L $path ]] || fail "unsafe or missing directory component: $path"
    done
}

metadata_dir() {
    safe_dir_chain '@'
    safe_dir_chain '@/usr'
    safe_dir_chain '@/usr/share'
    safe_dir_chain '@/usr/share/op-dbus'
    IMAGE=$TOP/$IMAGE_REL
    [[ -d $IMAGE && ! -L $IMAGE ]] || fail 'image metadata directory is missing or unsafe'
}

prepare_metadata_parent() {
    local path=$TOP component
    IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<< '@/usr/share/op-dbus'
    for component in "${parts[@]}"; do
        path=$path/$component
        if [[ -e $path || -L $path ]]; then
            [[ -d $path && ! -L $path ]] || fail "refusing symlink or non-directory metadata parent: $path"
        else
            mkdir -- "$path" || fail "cannot create metadata parent: $path"
            chmod 0755 -- "$path"
        fi
    done
    IMAGE=$path/image
}

hash_file() {
    local file=$1 value
    [[ -f $file && ! -L $file ]] || fail "expected ordinary file: $file"
    value=$(sha256sum -- "$file") || fail "cannot hash $file"
    printf '%s' "${value%% *}"
}

within_guest() {
    local path=$1 resolved
    [[ -e $path || -L $path ]] || fail "missing critical path: ${path#"$GUEST"/}"
    resolved=$(resolve_guest_path "${path#"$GUEST"/}") || fail "cannot resolve critical path inside guest root: $path"
    [[ -f $resolved ]] || fail "critical path does not resolve to a regular file: $path"
}

# Resolve symlinks using guest-root semantics. Host realpath follows absolute
# guest symlinks from the host's /, which both rejects valid links and risks
# hashing a host file. Absolute targets here restart at GUEST instead.
resolve_guest_path() {
    local rel=$1 component candidate target target_rel resolved_rel
    local -a todo=() target_parts=() stack=()
    local links=0 index
    [[ $rel != /* ]] || return 1
    IFS=/ read -r -a todo <<< "$rel"
    while ((${#todo[@]})); do
        component=${todo[0]}
        todo=("${todo[@]:1}")
        case $component in
            ''|.) continue ;;
            ..)
                ((${#stack[@]})) || return 1
                stack=("${stack[@]:0:${#stack[@]}-1}")
                continue
                ;;
        esac
        resolved_rel=$(IFS=/; printf '%s' "${stack[*]}")
        candidate=$GUEST
        [[ -z $resolved_rel ]] || candidate=$candidate/$resolved_rel
        candidate=$candidate/$component
        if [[ -L $candidate ]]; then
            ((links+=1))
            ((links <= 40)) || return 1
            target=$(readlink -- "$candidate") || return 1
            target_rel=$target
            if [[ $target == /* ]]; then
                stack=()
                target_rel=${target#/}
            fi
            IFS=/ read -r -a target_parts <<< "$target_rel"
            todo=("${target_parts[@]}" "${todo[@]}")
            continue
        fi
        if ((${#todo[@]})) && [[ ! -d $candidate ]]; then return 1; fi
        stack+=("$component")
    done
    resolved_rel=$(IFS=/; printf '%s' "${stack[*]}")
    [[ -n $resolved_rel ]] || return 1
    printf '%s/%s\n' "$GUEST" "$resolved_rel"
}

prepare_mountpoint_dirs() {
    local rel path component
    local -a parts=()
    for rel in run run/mount run/mount/3tchedfs run/opdbus run/opdbus/lungs; do
        path=$GUEST
        IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<< "$rel"
        for component in "${parts[@]}"; do
            path=$path/$component
            if [[ -e $path || -L $path ]]; then
                [[ -d $path && ! -L $path ]] || fail "refusing symlink or non-directory guest runtime path: $path"
            else
                mkdir -m 0755 -- "$path" || fail "cannot create guest runtime directory: $path"
            fi
            chown 0:0 -- "$path" || fail "cannot set guest runtime directory owner: $path"
            chmod 0755 -- "$path" || fail "cannot set guest runtime directory mode: $path"
        done
    done
}

critical_file_records() {
    local rel path resolved hash link target
    local records='{}'
    for rel in "${CRITICAL_PATHS[@]}"; do
        path=$GUEST/$rel
        within_guest "$path"
        resolved=$(resolve_guest_path "$rel") || fail "cannot resolve critical path inside guest root: $path"
        hash=$(hash_file "$resolved")
        link=''
        if [[ -L $path ]]; then link=$(readlink -- "$path"); fi
        records=$(jq -cn --argjson old "$records" --arg rel "$rel" --arg sha "$hash" --arg link "$link" \
            '$old + {($rel):{sha256:$sha,symlink_target:$link}}')
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$records"
}

extract_os_release() {
    local key=$1 release_file
    release_file=$(resolve_guest_path etc/os-release) || fail 'cannot resolve guest OS release file'
    [[ -f $release_file && ! -L $release_file ]] || fail 'guest OS release is not a regular file'
    awk -F= -v key="$key" '$1 == key {value=substr($0, length(key)+2); if (value ~ /^".*"$/ || value ~ /^\047.*\047$/) value=substr(value,2,length(value)-2); print value; exit}' "$release_file"
}

neutral_defaults() {
    local machine=empty hostname=absent name=''
    if [[ -e $GUEST/etc/machine-id || -L $GUEST/etc/machine-id ]]; then
        [[ -f $GUEST/etc/machine-id && ! -L $GUEST/etc/machine-id ]] || fail '/etc/machine-id must be absent or an ordinary empty file before sealing'
        [[ ! -s $GUEST/etc/machine-id ]] || fail '/etc/machine-id is not neutral; preserve it for operator review'
    else
        machine=absent
    fi
    if [[ -e $GUEST/etc/hostname || -L $GUEST/etc/hostname ]]; then
        [[ -f $GUEST/etc/hostname && ! -L $GUEST/etc/hostname ]] || fail '/etc/hostname must be an ordinary file before sealing'
        name=$(tr -d '\r\n' < "$GUEST/etc/hostname")
        case "$name" in ''|localhost|localhost.localdomain|ubuntu) ;; *) fail '/etc/hostname contains a non-neutral value; preserve it for operator review' ;; esac
        hostname=$name
    fi
    if [[ -d $GUEST/etc/ssh ]]; then
        [[ -z $(find "$GUEST/etc/ssh" -maxdepth 1 \( -type f -o -type l \) -name 'ssh_host_*' -print -quit) ]] || fail 'SSH host keys exist in the shared base; preserve them for operator review'
    fi
    jq -cn --arg machine "$machine" --arg hostname "$hostname" \
        '{machine_id:$machine,hostname:$hostname,ssh_host_keys:"absent"}'
}

package_inventory() {
    local status=$GUEST/var/lib/dpkg/status tmp=$1
    [[ -f $status && ! -L $status ]] || fail 'complete offline dpkg status database is missing'
    awk '
        BEGIN { RS=""; FS="\n"; bad=0 }
        {
            package=""; version=""; installed=0
            for (i=1; i<=NF; i++) {
                if (substr($i,1,9)=="Package: ") package=substr($i,10)
                else if (substr($i,1,9)=="Version: ") version=substr($i,10)
                else if ($i=="Status: install ok installed") installed=1
            }
            if (installed) {
                if (package=="" || version=="" || package ~ /[\t\r\n ]/ || version ~ /[\t\r\n ]/) bad=1
                else print package "\t" version
            }
        }
        END { if (bad) exit 3 }
    ' "$status" | LC_ALL=C sort -t "$(printf '\t')" -k1,1 > "$tmp" || fail 'dpkg status database has incomplete installed-package records'
    [[ -s $tmp ]] || fail 'dpkg status database contains no installed package records'
    [[ $(cut -f1 "$tmp" | uniq -d | wc -l) -eq 0 ]] || fail 'duplicate package names in installed-package inventory'
}

check_layout() {
    local actual expected name
    command -v btrfs >/dev/null || fail 'btrfs-progs is required for full layout verification'
    actual=$(btrfs subvolume list "$TOP" | sed -n 's/^.* path //p' | LC_ALL=C sort) || fail 'cannot list Btrfs subvolumes under TOP'
    expected=$(printf '%s\n' $MEMBERS | LC_ALL=C sort)
    [[ $actual == "$expected" ]] || fail 'TOP must contain exactly the seven declared flat sibling subvolumes'
    for name in $MEMBERS; do [[ -d $TOP/$name && ! -L $TOP/$name ]] || fail "missing or unsafe sibling: $name"; done
}

layout_json() {
    jq -cn --arg layout "$LAYOUT" '
      {layout:$layout,
       members:[
         {subvolume:"@",mountpoint:"/",guest_mode:"rw"},
         {subvolume:"@agent_memory",mountpoint:"/agent/memory",guest_mode:"rw"},
         {subvolume:"@agent_rules",mountpoint:"/agent/rules",guest_mode:"rw"},
         {subvolume:"@agent_shared",mountpoint:"/agent/shared",guest_mode:"ro"},
         {subvolume:"@agent_skills",mountpoint:"/agent/skills",guest_mode:"rw"},
         {subvolume:"@agent_soul",mountpoint:"/agent/soul",guest_mode:"ro"},
         {subvolume:"@agent_user",mountpoint:"/agent/user",guest_mode:"rw"}
       ],
       persistence:{source:"@agent_user/persist",kind:"ordinary-directory",guest_mountpoint:"/opt/run-mounts/persist",guest_mode:"rw"},
       runtime_mounts:[
         {path:"/run",owner:"incus-profile:3tched-lungs",filesystem:"tmpfs",lifetime:"per-start",seed_storage:false},
         {path:"/run/opdbus/lungs",source:"/run/opdbus/lungs",owner:"incus-profile:3tched-lungs",filesystem:"bind",guest_mode:"ro",lifetime:"per-start",seed_storage:false},
         {path:"/run/mount/3tchedfs",owner:"guest:3tchedfs.service",filesystem:"fuse.3tchedFS",lifetime:"per-start",seed_storage:false},
         {path:"/dev/shm/opdbus-physical-lungs/<native-session-uuid>",owner:"host",filesystem:"tmpfs",lifetime:"per-boot",seed_storage:false}
       ]}'
}

layout_check_json() {
    local file=$IMAGE/layout.json expected actual

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
IFS=$'\n\t'

LAYOUT=shared-partition-siblings-v2
SCHEMA_VERSION=1
IMAGE_REL=@/usr/share/op-dbus/image
MEMBERS=$'@\n@agent_memory\n@agent_rules\n@agent_shared\n@agent_skills\n@agent_soul\n@agent_user'
ARTIFACTS=(release.json provenance.json layout.json packages.tsv components.tsv critical-files.json critical-files.sha256 maintenance.txt)
CRITICAL_PATHS=(etc/os-release etc/fstab usr/lib/systemd/systemd usr/sbin/init)
REQUIRED_COMPONENTS=(base-files dpkg systemd systemd-sysv)

fail() { printf 'op-identity-image: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
usage() {
    cat >&2 <<'EOF'
Usage:
  op-identity-image prepare TOP RELEASE_ID PROVENANCE_JSON
  op-identity-image verify TOP
  op-identity-image verify-metadata TOP
  op-identity-image inspect TOP

TOP is an already mounted Btrfs top-level directory containing exactly the
seven shared workspace sibling subvolumes. prepare writes image metadata and
two runtime mountpoint directories inside @; it never mounts, formats, changes
seeding state, copies a root tree, or creates a subvolume.
EOF
    exit 2
}

canonical_top() {
    local input=$1 resolved
    [[ -d $input && ! -L $input ]] || fail "TOP must be an existing ordinary directory: $input"
    resolved=$(realpath -e -- "$input") || fail "cannot resolve TOP"
    [[ $resolved == "$input" && $resolved != / ]] || fail "TOP must be an absolute canonical path other than /"
    TOP=$resolved
    GUEST=$TOP/@
    [[ -d $GUEST && ! -L $GUEST ]] || fail "TOP/@ must be an ordinary guest root directory"
}

safe_dir_chain() {
    local rel=$1 path=$TOP component
    IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<< "$rel"
    for component in "${parts[@]}"; do
        path=$path/$component
        [[ -d $path && ! -L $path ]] || fail "unsafe or missing directory component: $path"
    done
}

metadata_dir() {
    safe_dir_chain '@'
    safe_dir_chain '@/usr'
    safe_dir_chain '@/usr/share'
    safe_dir_chain '@/usr/share/op-dbus'
    IMAGE=$TOP/$IMAGE_REL
    [[ -d $IMAGE && ! -L $IMAGE ]] || fail 'image metadata directory is missing or unsafe'
}

prepare_metadata_parent() {
    local path=$TOP component
    IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<< '@/usr/share/op-dbus'
    for component in "${parts[@]}"; do
        path=$path/$component
        if [[ -e $path || -L $path ]]; then
            [[ -d $path && ! -L $path ]] || fail "refusing symlink or non-directory metadata parent: $path"
        else
            mkdir -- "$path" || fail "cannot create metadata parent: $path"
            chmod 0755 -- "$path"
        fi
    done
    IMAGE=$path/image
}

hash_file() {
    local file=$1 value
    [[ -f $file && ! -L $file ]] || fail "expected ordinary file: $file"
    value=$(sha256sum -- "$file") || fail "cannot hash $file"
    printf '%s' "${value%% *}"
}

within_guest() {
    local path=$1 resolved
    [[ -e $path || -L $path ]] || fail "missing critical path: ${path#"$GUEST"/}"
    resolved=$(resolve_guest_path "${path#"$GUEST"/}") || fail "cannot resolve critical path inside guest root: $path"
    [[ -f $resolved ]] || fail "critical path does not resolve to a regular file: $path"
}

# Resolve symlinks using guest-root semantics. Host realpath follows absolute
# guest symlinks from the host's /, which both rejects valid links and risks
# hashing a host file. Absolute targets here restart at GUEST instead.
resolve_guest_path() {
    local rel=$1 component candidate target target_rel resolved_rel
    local -a todo=() target_parts=() stack=()
    local links=0 index
    [[ $rel != /* ]] || return 1
    IFS=/ read -r -a todo <<< "$rel"
    while ((${#todo[@]})); do
        component=${todo[0]}
        todo=("${todo[@]:1}")
        case $component in
            ''|.) continue ;;
            ..)
                ((${#stack[@]})) || return 1
                stack=("${stack[@]:0:${#stack[@]}-1}")
                continue
                ;;
        esac
        resolved_rel=$(IFS=/; printf '%s' "${stack[*]}")
        candidate=$GUEST
        [[ -z $resolved_rel ]] || candidate=$candidate/$resolved_rel
        candidate=$candidate/$component
        if [[ -L $candidate ]]; then
            ((links+=1))
            ((links <= 40)) || return 1
            target=$(readlink -- "$candidate") || return 1
            target_rel=$target
            if [[ $target == /* ]]; then
                stack=()
                target_rel=${target#/}
            fi
            IFS=/ read -r -a target_parts <<< "$target_rel"
            todo=("${target_parts[@]}" "${todo[@]}")
            continue
        fi
        if ((${#todo[@]})) && [[ ! -d $candidate ]]; then return 1; fi
        stack+=("$component")
    done
    resolved_rel=$(IFS=/; printf '%s' "${stack[*]}")
    [[ -n $resolved_rel ]] || return 1
    printf '%s/%s\n' "$GUEST" "$resolved_rel"
}

prepare_mountpoint_dirs() {
    local rel path component
    local -a parts=()
    for rel in run run/mount run/mount/3tchedfs run/opdbus run/opdbus/lungs; do
        path=$GUEST
        IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<< "$rel"
        for component in "${parts[@]}"; do
            path=$path/$component
            if [[ -e $path || -L $path ]]; then
                [[ -d $path && ! -L $path ]] || fail "refusing symlink or non-directory guest runtime path: $path"
            else
                mkdir -m 0755 -- "$path" || fail "cannot create guest runtime directory: $path"
            fi
            chown 0:0 -- "$path" || fail "cannot set guest runtime directory owner: $path"
            chmod 0755 -- "$path" || fail "cannot set guest runtime directory mode: $path"
        done
    done
}

critical_file_records() {
    local rel path resolved hash link target
    local records='{}'
    for rel in "${CRITICAL_PATHS[@]}"; do
        path=$GUEST/$rel
        within_guest "$path"
        resolved=$(resolve_guest_path "$rel") || fail "cannot resolve critical path inside guest root: $path"
        hash=$(hash_file "$resolved")
        link=''
        if [[ -L $path ]]; then link=$(readlink -- "$path"); fi
        records=$(jq -cn --argjson old "$records" --arg rel "$rel" --arg sha "$hash" --arg link "$link" \
            '$old + {($rel):{sha256:$sha,symlink_target:$link}}')
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$records"
}

extract_os_release() {
    local key=$1 release_file
    release_file=$(resolve_guest_path etc/os-release) || fail 'cannot resolve guest OS release file'
    [[ -f $release_file && ! -L $release_file ]] || fail 'guest OS release is not a regular file'
    awk -F= -v key="$key" '$1 == key {value=substr($0, length(key)+2); if (value ~ /^".*"$/ || value ~ /^\047.*\047$/) value=substr(value,2,length(value)-2); print value; exit}' "$release_file"
}

neutral_defaults() {
    local machine=empty hostname=absent name=''
    if [[ -e $GUEST/etc/machine-id || -L $GUEST/etc/machine-id ]]; then
        [[ -f $GUEST/etc/machine-id && ! -L $GUEST/etc/machine-id ]] || fail '/etc/machine-id must be absent or an ordinary empty file before sealing'
        [[ ! -s $GUEST/etc/machine-id ]] || fail '/etc/machine-id is not neutral; preserve it for operator review'

    if [[ -e $GUEST/etc/hostname || -L $GUEST/etc/hostname ]]; then

package_inventory() {

}

    jq -cnS --arg release "$release_id" --arg layout "$LAYOUT" \
       --argjson version "$SCHEMA_VERSION" --argjson count "$package_count" \
       --argjson critical "$critical" --argjson defaults "$defaults" \
       --argjson artifacts "$artifact_hashes" \
       '{schema_version:$version,release_id:$release,layout:$layout,package_count:$count,critical_files:$critical,neutral_defaults:$defaults,artifact_sha256:$artifacts}' \
       > "$IMAGE/manifest.json"
    chmod 0444 -- "$IMAGE/manifest.json"
    # Validate the just-created metadata and the complete unsealed tree.
    verify_full >/dev/null
    printf 'prepared image metadata under %s\n' "$IMAGE"
}

main() {
    [[ $# -ge 1 ]] || usage
    local command=$1
    shift
    case "$command" in
        prepare)
            [[ $# -eq 3 ]] || usage
            canonical_top "$1"

        verify)

    done

    critical=$(critical_file_records)
    printf '%s\n' "$critical" > "$IMAGE/critical-files.json"
    chmod 0444 -- "$IMAGE/components.tsv" "$IMAGE/critical-files.json"
    cat > "$IMAGE/maintenance.txt" <<'EOF'
This is immutable shared-seed provenance and layout metadata. Keep the seed
unchanged while any sprout depends on it. Updating the seed in place invalidates
existing sprouts. Do not store session identity, credentials, SSH host keys,
machine IDs, or per-container runtime state in the seed. Prepare recovery tools

    layout=$(jq -cS . "$IMAGE/layout.json")

$(jq -r 'to_entries|sort_by(.key)[]|"\(.value.sha256)  \(.key)"' <<<"$critical")

       --argjson artifacts "$artifact_hashes" \

    local command=$1
    shift
    case "$command" in

            prepare "$2" "$3"

            metadata_dir

            canonical_top "$1"
            metadata_dir
            verify_full >/dev/null

}

  host owner, mounts inherited siblings, attaches the Incus socket profile,
  host folders and FUSE, then calls supported clean provisioning with a pinned
  root-owned plan. The normal flow starts through `touch_session` and records
  boot completion only after authoritative and native readback.

  publication. Private historical receipts are not imported into the new

  removes Btrfs devices.

  held namespaces, native UUID and init process, with revalidation on every

  does not grant plugin capability.

  native ID mapping rather than an automatic recursive ownership rewrite.
  Read-only evidence from current Xray and Sept30 seed fixtures supports this
  mechanism; it is not a substitute for the fresh container's first start.

  schema-only view into the existing base before image metadata/sealing. FUSE

    if findmnt -rn -M "$layer" >/dev/null; then umount "$layer"; fi
done
generation=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)-$$
parent=$(jq -r '.generation // empty' "$state")
jq --arg next "$generation" '.phase="send-intent"|.next_generation=$next' "$state" > "$state.new"
mv -T "$state.new" "$state"
sync -f "$pool/.provisioning"
btrfs subvolume snapshot -r "$host/@" "$source_snapshots/$generation"
if [[ -n $parent ]]; then
    [[ $(btrfs property get -ts "$source_snapshots/$parent" ro) == 'ro=true' && $(btrfs property get -ts "$received/$parent" ro) == 'ro=true' ]] || fail 'immutable common baseline missing'
    btrfs send -p "$source_snapshots/$parent" "$source_snapshots/$generation" | btrfs receive "$received"
else
    btrfs send "$source_snapshots/$generation" | btrfs receive "$received"
fi
sent_uuid=$(btrfs subvolume show "$source_snapshots/$generation" | awk '$1=="UUID:" {print $2}')
received_uuid=$(btrfs subvolume show "$received/$generation" | awk '$1=="Received" && $2=="UUID:" {print $3}')
[[ -n $sent_uuid && $sent_uuid == "$received_uuid" && $(btrfs property get -ts "$received/$generation" ro) == 'ro=true' ]] || fail 'receive identity/read-only receipt differs'
# Keep received snapshots immutable for future incremental sends. @ is a
# writable clone; the exposed root view, not this upgrade partition, is RO.
btrfs subvolume snapshot "$received/$generation" "$replica/.next-$generation"
mv "$replica/@" "$received/previous-$generation"
mv "$replica/.next-$generation" "$replica/@"
sync -f "$host"
sync -f "$replica"
jq --arg generation "$generation" '.phase="paired"|.generation=$generation|del(.next_generation)' "$state" > "$state.new"
mv -T "$state.new" "$state"
sync -f "$pool/.provisioning"
if [[ $action == boot ]]; then
    # Both OS layers are read-only in the guest. The upgrade partition itself
    # remains writable for receive/rotation; user siblings are separate binds.
    # Patches deleting seed files must carry whiteouts in the upgrade layer.
    instance=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$name")
    jq -e '.status=="Stopped" and .config["security.privileged"]=="false" and
        .config["security.protection.shift"]=="true" and .devices.root.pool=="identity-roots"' \
        <<<"$instance" >/dev/null || fail 'stopped identity container required for boot mounts'
    idmap=$(jq -er '.config["volatile.idmap.current"]' <<<"$instance")
    jq -e 'length==2 and all(.[]; .Hostid==1000000 and .Nsid==0 and .Maprange==1000000000) and
        any(.[]; .Isuid==true and .Isgid==false) and any(.[]; .Isgid==true and .Isuid==false)' \
        <<<"$idmap" >/dev/null || fail 'unsupported identity idmap'
    [[ -d $container_root && ! -L $container_root &&
       $(realpath -e "$container_root") == "$container_root" ]] || fail 'unsafe Incus root path'
    mkdir -p "$view" "$seed_layer" "$upgrade_layer"
    # This kernel cannot idmap an OverlayFS mount. Map its Btrfs lowers first.
    mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@" "$seed_layer"
    mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$replica/@" "$upgrade_layer"
    mount -t overlay overlay -o "ro,lowerdir=$upgrade_layer:$seed_layer" "$view"
    for member in memory rules shared skills soul user; do
        [[ -d $view/agent/$member && ! -L $view/agent/$member ]] || fail "upgrade missing /agent/$member"
        mount --bind -o X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@agent_$member" "$view/agent/$member"
        case "$member" in shared|soul) mount -o remount,bind,ro "$view/agent/$member" ;; esac
    done
    mount --bind -o X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@agent_user/persist" "$view/opt/run-mounts/persist"
    mount --rbind "$view" "$container_root"
    incus config set "$name" "volatile.last_state.idmap=$idmap"
fi
printf 'Upgrade synchronized host -> %s; user data excluded.\n' "$name"

# Shared physical seed and private leaves
…
The bridge service creates its existing shared socket at
…
rejects local overrides. The `/run` tmpfs is mounted before its child devices;
image directories alone would not establish that boot ordering.

The bridge creates a root-owned socket with mode 0666 beneath the root-owned
0755 directory. Connection permission allows negotiation; each operation still
requires an authenticated identity and its existing capability grant. Host
`Bind(session)` requires UID 0 in the bridge's own user and PID namespaces.
Guest `BindCurrentContainer()` takes no session argument: it pins the socket's
original process with SO_PEERPIDFD and derives identity from the exact running
native container. Process, native UUID and authoritative identity are checked
again for each call. No SID1 file is installed in the guest.

Clean replacement is scoped to the configured chatbot key and service identity
`b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`, using the provisioner's configured native
alias `3tchedCtlbot`. Hostname remains the session UUID. The old native instance
must be stopped or authoritatively absent, and the new name and leaf must be
unused. Explicit retirement uses `identity_sled.delete_provision_record` through
the operator's mounted namespace, with the existing human write capability
and exact revision. This removes the current row and retains an audit tombstone;
startup respects that tombstone. A version3 plan permits fresh provisioning
from that exact deletion receipt. Ordinary missing rows are not accepted.
After host storage/mount
preparation, the wrapper submits a digest-pinned private plan through the
supported `identity_sled.provision_container` operation. The owner atomically
creates fresh current-schema state and binds it to the new native instance;
legacy persistence and record fields are not imported. Existing external
capability policy remains in force. Normal provisioning starts through
`touch_session`; `--no-start` leaves the fresh identity parked. Only verified
completion receives a boot-ready marker.

If creation fails, `op-identity-root seed-inspect NAME` reports sanitized
receipt metadata and recovery guidance without mounting, formatting or
retrying device-add. Preserve the receipt, base, leaf and mappings until the
recorded intent and actual membership have been reconciled.

Preparing or changing the live seed is a separate operator action. The helper
does not set or clear SEEDING, format the partition, or unmount an unrelated
source mount. Once leaves depend on a seed, that seed must remain unchanged.
At boot, the host storage service uses `seed-readonly` to verify the physical
partition identity and existing SEEDING state, then restore its volatile block
read-only flag before restoring opted-in roots. This never changes filesystem
membership or the SEEDING flag.
The current source change has not been deployed or validated with concurrent
live containers on the fresh base. The September 30 file-backed and physical
seed experiments did demonstrate independent writes, peer-active remounts and
cold loop recreation using distinct read-only views of the same seed on this
kernel. That evidence does not validate this new image/layout or a full host
reboot. There is no fallback to copied seeds if a kernel rejects the shared
arrangement. The owner's current sequencing instruction defers all tests until
after deployment; a successful build alone is not a workflow validation.

See the [Btrfs seeding documentation](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Seeding-device.html).

#!/bin/sh
# Host storage owner: remount/receive existing GPT members, never mint/start.
set -eu
pool=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool
receipt=$pool/.provisioning/3tchedChatbot.boot.json
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ]
[ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSROOT)" = /@3tched-leaf-pool ]
[ -f "$receipt" ] && [ ! -L "$receipt" ]
[ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a "$receipt")" = 0:0:600 ]
jq -e '.version==1 and .name=="3tchedChatbot" and
    .session_id=="b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28" and
    .identity_registered==true and .restore_existing_pair==true' "$receipt" >/dev/null
state=$(incus --force-local query /1.0/instances/3tchedChatbot/state | jq -er .status)
root=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots/containers/3tchedChatbot/rootfs
case "$state" in
    Stopped) /usr/local/libexec/3tched/sync-instance-upgrade boot 3tchedChatbot ;;
    Running)
        # A service restart must not replace a running container's lowers.
        [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o FSTYPE)" = overlay ]
        case ",$(findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o OPTIONS)," in *,ro,*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
        ;;
    *) echo "unsupported chatbot state: $state" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

## Summary

**There are three materially different versions to export: historical working stages, installed helpers/base boot wiring, and today’s partially edited source. They are not interchangeable.**

Most important current findings:

1. **The source chain is internally inconsistent.** Most edited GPT helpers now require `/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/3tched-pool` and upgrade FSID `7ac6c955-4028-439c-80b4-c55a647abcb4`; `sync-instance-upgrade.sh` still requires `/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool` and `5a88e7cd-9701-40a7-8301-ef076761886c`.
2. **Installed base boot wiring is older than the installed application helper closure.** I directly read `/etc/sv/identity-roots/run`: it still selects only `3tchedChatbot.boot.json` under the old pool, invokes `/usr/local/libexec/3tched/*`, then exits into `sleep infinity`, suppressing subsequent identity restoration. This independently confirms a remaining installed form of audit F10—not merely a stale handoff.
3. **Neither original `op-identity-root` nor current GPT helpers implement loop-free native Incus container volumes.** Both installed versions of `op-identity-root` explicitly allocate seed and leaf loops. Current adoption proof explicitly requires GPT loop partitions.
4. **Oct5 “working” needs qualification:** native container/root writes were reported working, but the scripted candidate receipt and manually assembled leaf were different and unreconciled. **Oct11 has stronger historical evidence:** successful canonical start and guest identity receipt, followed by deployed boot wiring; actual cold reboot remained unexercised.
5. **Hermes explicitly acknowledged drift**, including unnecessary naming-related boot restrictions, presenting unfinished checks as blockers, conflating persistent storage with an overlay upper, and auditing pieces rather than the requested complete provisioning chain. Exact message references below.

All work here was read-only. No scripts, tests, builds, native operations, or privileged bypass were executed.

# Attach the bridge's shared lungs socket to one identity.
#
# The socket is the only thing the host puts in place. The identity mounts its
# own 3tchedFS from inside, through the seed's `3tchedfs.service`, so the view
# is rendered in the identity's own namespace instead of being a host mount
# handed across the boundary.
#
# One socket serves every identity: a Unix socket's identity is per
# connection, and the bridge resolves each accepted peer to exactly one
# running committed container. The guest therefore passes no session argument
# — it calls BindCurrentContainer() and the kernel names it.
attach_lungs_socket() {
    session=$1
    [ -S "$LUNGS_SOCKET" ] || { log "$session: bridge lungs socket absent"; return 1; }
    # A directory bind, not the socket file: the bridge may recreate the
    # socket on restart, and a file bind would pin the old inode.
    socket_dir=$(dirname "$LUNGS_SOCKET")
    guest_dir=$(dirname "$GUEST_LUNGS_SOCKET")
    case "$socket_dir:$guest_dir" in
        /:*|/run:*|*:/|*:/run)
            log "$session: lungs requires dedicated host and guest socket directories"
            return 1
            ;;
    esac
    if incus config device get "$session" lungs source >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        incus config device set "$session" lungs \
            source="$socket_dir" path="$guest_dir" readonly=true
    else
        incus config device add "$session" lungs disk \
            source="$socket_dir" path="$guest_dir" readonly=true >/dev/null
    fi
}

# Remove a retired host-side lungs mount and its Incus disk device.
#
# Earlier releases mounted 3tchedFS on the host per session and bound that
# mount in at /opt/run-mounts/3tched. Identities that were provisioned then
# still carry the device, so starting one would otherwise keep the host mount
# alive beside the in-guest one.
retire_host_lungs_mount() {
    session=$1
    if incus config device get "$session" 3tched source >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        incus config device remove "$session" 3tched >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
            log "$session: could not remove the retired 3tched disk device"
    fi
    mountpoint -q "$LUNGS_RUN/$session" && umount "$LUNGS_RUN/$session"
    return 0
}

up_one() {
    session=$1
    valid_session "$session" || { log "skipping '$session': not a session id"; return 1; }
    validate_identity_container "$session" || return 1
    validate_network_devices "$session" || return 1
    validate_seed_defaults || return 1
    mount_device "$session" || { log "$session: device failed"; return 1; }
    ensure_soul "$session" || log "$session: soul subvolumes failed"
    mount_root "$session" || { log "$session: root overlay failed"; return 1; }
    retire_host_lungs_mount "$session"
    if attach_lungs_socket "$session"; then
        log "$session: lungs socket attached at $GUEST_LUNGS_SOCKET"
    else
        log "$session: lungs socket unavailable; identity starts without them"
    fi
    if container_running "$session"; then
        return 0
    fi
…
}

    i=0

    [[ $(id -u) == 0 ]] || die 'container preparation requires host root'

        'ioctl errno 1 [1,0x4008941a,SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ,0xffffffff]' \
        'ioctl errno 1 [1,0x5000940f,SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ,0xffffffff]' \
        'ioctl errno 1 [1,0x5000943f,SCMP_CMP_MASKED_EQ,0xffffffff]')

        --config security.privileged=false --config security.nesting=false \
        --config security.protection.shift=true --config boot.autostart=false \
        --config security.syscalls.deny_default=true --config "security.syscalls.deny=$deny_policy" \

    incus config device override "$1" runtime-run

    mv -T "$container_receipt.new" "$container_receipt"
    sync -f "$pool_root/.provisioning"

)

    --prepare-adoption)
        shift
        script_dir=$(dirname -- "$(realpath -e -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")
        adoption_helper=$script_dir/prepare-chatbot-adoption.sh
        [[ -x $adoption_helper ]] || adoption_helper=$script_dir/prepare-chatbot-adoption
        [[ -x $adoption_helper ]] || die 'adoption plan helper missing'
        exec "$adoption_helper" "$@"
        ;;
    --bind-root)
        shift
        script_dir=$(dirname -- "$(realpath -e -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")
        bind_helper=$script_dir/bind-instance-root.sh
        [[ -x $bind_helper ]] || bind_helper=$script_dir/bind-instance-root
        [[ -x $bind_helper ]] || die 'root binding helper missing'
        exec "$bind_helper" "$@"
        ;;

        shift
        prepare_chatbot_container "$@"

ensure_soul() {
…
    for name in truths boundaries vibe; do
        path=$cozo/$name
        [ -d "$path" ] && [ ! -L "$path" ] && btrfs subvolume show "$path" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
            log "$session: existing soul subvolume missing: $name"; return 1;
        }
        [ "$(incus config device get "$session" "soul-$name" source)" = "$path" ] &&
            [ "$(incus config device get "$session" "soul-$name" path)" = "/soul/$name" ] &&
            [ "$(incus config device get "$session" "soul-$name" readonly)" = true ] || return 1
    done
}

mount_device() {
    session=$1
    dir=$IDENTITIES/$session
    image=$dir/identity.img
    [ -f "$image" ] || { log "$session: no identity device"; return 1; }
    mountpoint -q "$dir/device" && return 0
    loop=$(loop_for "$image")
    [ -n "$loop" ] || loop=$(losetup -f --show "$image") || return 1
    label=$(blkid -s LABEL -o value "$loop" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ "$label" != "identity-$session" ]; then
        log "$session: device label '$label' does not name this identity"
        losetup -d "$loop" 2>/dev/null
        return 1
    fi
    install -d -m 0700 "$dir/device"
    mount -o noatime "$loop" "$dir/device"
}

mount_root() {
    session=$1
    dir=$IDENTITIES/$session/device
    root=$POOL_PATH/$session/rootfs
    [ -d "$root" ] || { log "$session: no Incus instance on pool $POOL"; return 1; }
    mountpoint -q "$root" && return 0
    mount -t overlay overlay \
        -o "lowerdir=$SEEDS_IDMAP,upperdir=$dir/upper,workdir=$dir/work" "$root"
}

mount_lungs() {
    session=$1
    lungs=$LUNGS_RUN/$session
    mountpoint -q "$lungs" && return 0
…
}
…
# Raccoon. The identity's keys (user.opdbus.*) come from its current Incus
# instance, which is renamed <session>-archived-<date>, never deleted, so the
# old root and its devices stay available for rollback. Nothing is minted:
# the session, its sled and its principal already exist.
create_one() {
    session=$1
    size=$2
    valid_session "$session" || { log "'$session' is not a session id"; return 2; }
    dir=$IDENTITIES/$session
    [ -e "$dir/identity.img" ] && { log "$session: already has a device"; return 1; }
    [ -d "$POOL_PATH/$session" ] && { log "$session: already on pool $POOL"; return 1; }
    incus info "$session" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "$session: no Incus instance to take keys from"; return 1; }
    validate_identity_container "$session" || return 1
    validate_network_devices "$session" || return 1
    validate_seed_defaults || return 1
    keys=$(incus config show "$session" | sed -n 's/^  \(user\.opdbus\.[a-z_]*\): \(.*\)$/\1=\2/p')
    printf '%s\n' "$keys" | grep -q "^user.opdbus.session_id=$session$" ||
        { log "$session: instance does not carry its own session id"; return 1; }
    printf '%s\n' "$keys" | grep -q '^user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key=.' ||
        { log "$session: instance carries no WireGuard key"; return 1; }
    if [ "${ARCHIVE_EXISTING:-0}" != 1 ]; then
        log "$session: set ARCHIVE_EXISTING=1 to stop and rename the current instance"
        return 1
    fi
    archived=$session-archived-$(date -u +%Y%m%d)
    incus info "$archived" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { log "$archived already exists"; return 1; }

    incus stop "$session" --timeout 30 2>/dev/null || incus stop "$session" --force 2>/dev/null
    incus move "$session" "$archived" || { log "$session: rename failed"; return 1; }
    log "$session: previous instance kept as $archived"

    install -d -m 0700 "$dir" "$dir/device"
    truncate -s "$size" "$dir/identity.img"
    mkfs.btrfs -q -L "identity-$session" "$dir/identity.img" || return 1
    mount_device "$session" || return 1
    install -d -o 1000000 -g 1000000 -m 0755 "$dir/device/upper"
    install -d -m 0700 "$dir/device/work"
    install -d -o 1000000 -g 1000000 -m 0700 "$dir/device/cozo"

    incus init --empty "$session" --no-profiles -s "$POOL" >/dev/null || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$keys" | while IFS= read -r kv; do
        [ -n "$kv" ] && incus config set "$session" "$kv"
    done
    incus config set "$session" boot.autostart=false
    incus config set "$session" security.nesting=false
    incus config set "$session" "user.opdbus.identity_device=identity-$session"
    # Preset the idmap so Incus does not shift (copy) Raccoon into upper.
    incus config set "$session" volatile.last_state.idmap="$(incus config get "$session" volatile.idmap.next)"
    incus config device add "$session" ghostbridge-socket disk \
        source=/run/ghostbridge path=/opt/run-mounts/ghostbridge >/dev/null
    incus config device add "$session" persist disk \
        source="$dir/device/cozo" path=/opt/run-mounts/persist >/dev/null
    ensure_soul "$session" || { log "$session: soul subvolumes failed"; return 1; }
    log "$session: device and identity root created; run: $0 up $session"
}

            [ "$(incus config device get "$session" "soul-$name" path)" = "/soul/$name" ] &&
            [ "$(incus config device get "$session" "soul-$name" readonly)" = true ] || return 1
    done
}

mount_device() {
    session=$1
    dir=$IDENTITIES/$session
    image=$dir/identity.img
    [ -f "$image" ] || { log "$session: no identity device"; return 1; }
    mountpoint -q "$dir/device" && return 0
    loop=$(loop_for "$image")
    [ -n "$loop" ] || loop=$(losetup -f --show "$image") || return 1
    label=$(blkid -s LABEL -o value "$loop" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ "$label" != "identity-$session" ]; then
        log "$session: device label '$label' does not name this identity"
        losetup -d "$loop" 2>/dev/null
        return 1
    fi
    install -d -m 0700 "$dir/device"
    mount -o noatime "$loop" "$dir/device"
}

mount_root() {
    session=$1
    dir=$IDENTITIES/$session/device
    root=$POOL_PATH/$session/rootfs
    [ -d "$root" ] || { log "$session: no Incus instance on pool $POOL"; return 1; }
    mountpoint -q "$root" && return 0
    mount -t overlay overlay \
        -o "lowerdir=$SEEDS_IDMAP,upperdir=$dir/upper,workdir=$dir/work" "$root"
}

mount_lungs() {
    session=$1
    lungs=$LUNGS_RUN/$session
    mountpoint -q "$lungs" && return 0
…
}
…
# Raccoon. The identity's keys (user.opdbus.*) come from its current Incus
# instance, which is renamed <session>-archived-<date>, never deleted, so the
# old root and its devices stay available for rollback. Nothing is minted:
# the session, its sled and its principal already exist.
create_one() {
    session=$1
    size=$2
    valid_session "$session" || { log "'$session' is not a session id"; return 2; }
    dir=$IDENTITIES/$session
    [ -e "$dir/identity.img" ] && { log "$session: already has a device"; return 1; }
    [ -d "$POOL_PATH/$session" ] && { log "$session: already on pool $POOL"; return 1; }
    incus info "$session" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "$session: no Incus instance to take keys from"; return 1; }
    validate_identity_container "$session" || return 1
    validate_network_devices "$session" || return 1
    validate_seed_defaults || return 1
    keys=$(incus config show "$session" | sed -n 's/^  \(user\.opdbus\.[a-z_]*\): \(.*\)$/\1=\2/p')
    printf '%s\n' "$keys" | grep -q "^user.opdbus.session_id=$session$" ||
        { log "$session: instance does not carry its own session id"; return 1; }
    printf '%s\n' "$keys" | grep -q '^user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key=.' ||
        { log "$session: instance carries no WireGuard key"; return 1; }
    if [ "${ARCHIVE_EXISTING:-0}" != 1 ]; then
        log "$session: set ARCHIVE_EXISTING=1 to stop and rename the current instance"
        return 1
    fi
    archived=$session-archived-$(date -u +%Y%m%d)
    incus info "$archived" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { log "$archived already exists"; return 1; }

    incus stop "$session" --timeout 30 2>/dev/null || incus stop "$session" --force 2>/dev/null
    incus move "$session" "$archived" || { log "$session: rename failed"; return 1; }
    log "$session: previous instance kept as $archived"

    install -d -m 0700 "$dir" "$dir/device"
    truncate -s "$size" "$dir/identity.img"
    mkfs.btrfs -q -L "identity-$session" "$dir/identity.img" || return 1
    mount_device "$session" || return 1
    install -d -o 1000000 -g 1000000 -m 0755 "$dir/device/upper"
    install -d -m 0700 "$dir/device/work"
    install -d -o 1000000 -g 1000000 -m 0700 "$dir/device/cozo"

    incus init --empty "$session" --no-profiles -s "$POOL" >/dev/null || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$keys" | while IFS= read -r kv; do
        [ -n "$kv" ] && incus config set "$session" "$kv"
    done
    incus config set "$session" boot.autostart=false
    incus config set "$session" security.nesting=false
    incus config set "$session" "user.opdbus.identity_device=identity-$session"
    # Preset the idmap so Incus does not shift (copy) Raccoon into upper.
    incus config set "$session" volatile.last_state.idmap="$(incus config get "$session" volatile.idmap.next)"
    incus config device add "$session" ghostbridge-socket disk \
        source=/run/ghostbridge path=/opt/run-mounts/ghostbridge >/dev/null
    incus config device add "$session" persist disk \
        source="$dir/device/cozo" path=/opt/run-mounts/persist >/dev/null
    ensure_soul "$session" || { log "$session: soul subvolumes failed"; return 1; }
    log "$session: device and identity root created; run: $0 up $session"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Upgrade OS only: host -> instance; never replicate user/agent subvolumes.
set -euo pipefail
fail() { printf 'sync-instance-upgrade: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ $# == 2 && $1 =~ ^(pair|sync|boot)$ && $2 =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,62}$ ]] || fail 'usage: sync-instance-upgrade pair|sync|boot NAME'
action=$1 name=$2
[[ $(id -u) == 0 ]] || fail 'host root required'
incus() { command incus --force-local "$@"; }
for tool in jq btrfs blkid findmnt losetup mount umount flock incus stat realpath blockdev lsblk awk find head; do
    command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || fail "missing $tool"
done
umask 077
pool=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool
[[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSROOT) == /@3tched-leaf-pool ]] || fail 'leaf pool not mounted'
receipt=$pool/.provisioning/$name.json
[[ -f $receipt && ! -L $receipt ]] || fail 'preparation receipt required'
jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg image "$pool/$name.img" \
    '.phase=="filesystems-prepared" and .name==$name and .image==$image and .filesystem_prepared==true' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail 'disk not prepared'
image=$pool/$name.img
[[ -f $image && ! -L $image && $(stat -c %i "$image") == "$(jq -r .image_inode "$receipt")" && $(stat -c %s "$image") == "$(jq -r .image_bytes "$receipt")" ]] || fail 'image pins differ'
exec 8>"$pool/.provisioning/host-upgrade.lock"
flock -n 8 || fail 'host upgrade transfer active'
exec 9>"$pool/.provisioning/$name.lock"
flock -n 9 || fail 'instance preparation active'
instances=$(incus list -f json)
[[ $(jq --arg name "$name" '[.[]|select(.name==$name and .status!="Stopped")]|length' <<<"$instances") == 0 ]] || fail 'instance must be stopped'
root=$pool/.mounts/$name/root
replica=$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade
view=$pool/.mounts/$name/root-view
seed_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/seed-layer
upgrade_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade-layer
container_root=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots/containers/$name/rootfs
[[ $(jq -r .root_mount "$receipt") == "$root" && $(jq -r .upgrade_mount "$receipt") == "$replica" ]] || fail 'mount pins differ'
# Remount existing members after reboot, never add/remove a member or format.
if ! findmnt -rn -M "$root" >/dev/null || ! findmnt -rn -M "$replica" >/dev/null; then
    seed=$(jq -er .seed_device "$receipt")
    [[ $seed == /dev/disk/by-uuid/"$(jq -r .seed_fsid "$receipt")" && -b $seed ]] || fail 'seed unavailable'
    # UUID aliases can resolve to an already registered RO loop view.
    seed=$(lsblk -J -o PATH,TYPE,UUID | jq -er --arg uuid "$(jq -er .seed_fsid "$receipt")" \
        '[..|objects|select(.uuid==$uuid and .type=="part")|.path]|select(length==1)|.[0]') || fail 'physical seed is not unique'
    blockdev --setro "$seed"
    seed_loop=$(losetup -j "$(realpath -e "$seed")" -O NAME --noheadings | head -n 1)
    [[ -n $seed_loop ]] || seed_loop=$(losetup --find --show --read-only "$seed")
    [[ $(blockdev --getro "$seed_loop") == 1 ]] || fail 'seed loop must be read-only'
    disk_loop=$(losetup -j "$image" -O NAME --noheadings | head -n 1)
    [[ -n $disk_loop ]] || disk_loop=$(losetup --find --show --partscan "$image")
